News.title: Kim Jong-un deploys missile unit as he helps tyrant pal Putin with Ukraine war… & more soldiers are on their way
News.content:
ROCKET BUDDIES Kim Jong-un deploys missile unit as he helps tyrant pal Putin with Ukraine war… & more soldiers are on their way

NORTH Korea is dispatching missiles and troops to Russia, in a move which threatens to overwhelm Ukraine’s air-defences.

Kim Jong-un has promised 120 North Korean ballistic missiles and six launchers to Vladimir Putin, intelligence suggests.



With Ukraine in short supply of high-end air defences Russia is now trying to exploit this by deploying more ballistic missiles – which are notoriously hard to shoot down.

The advancement of North Korean missile forces represents an extension of the already extensive military cooperation between Moscow and Pyongyang.



Ukrainian intelligence officer Andrii Cherniak revealed Russia plans to deploy around 90 North Korean troops to a missile unit in Voronezh.

It is not clear what precise role the North Korean personnel would play in Russian missile operations.



Last month the Kremlin wanted North Korea to send another 30,000 troops and that Russian preparations were under way to receive them in the Voronezh region, according to Zelensky.

A source familiar with the issue said that the United States is aware of the recent North Korean deployment, but declined to elaborate.



This deployment comes hot on the heels of Russia firing its first two North Korean missiles at Ukraine since last August.

Russia has fired scores of North Korean ballistic missiles at Ukraine since late 2023.

Rob Lee, a senior fellow at the Foreign Policy Research Institute said the North Korean resources pose a significant threat for Kyiv.

He said: “Ballistic missile defence is one of Ukraine’s greatest vulnerabilities so any increase in the quantities of ballistic missiles they face will pose a greater challenge.”

Lee said a big concern for Ukraine will be the state of its air defences this winter, when Russia could again target the power grid as in past years.



North Korean missiles may be bigger than Russia’s but – importantly – they are far less precise.

Cherniak said last week’s strike was the first recorded attack using North Korean ballistic missiles since August 2025, and that it had drawn from the new batch of 40 missiles.

The use of North Korea‘s KN-23/24 missiles fits a pattern in which Russia has tried to use more ballistic missiles that can only be stopped by U.S.-made Patriot air defence systems.

North Korea supplied 150 of the missiles between the end of 2023 and August 2025, Cherniak said.

He said there were around 9,500 North Korean troops in Russia’s Kursk region, which borders Ukraine but that they were not currently directly involved in military operations against Ukraine.



North Korea has emerged as a close ally of Russia since Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and the two powers signed a mutual defence pact in 2024.

The move would be bolstering the estimated 14,000 North Korean personnel already deployed in the region.

It comes as Russia unleashed a barrage of missile and drone strikes on Kyiv – killing 17 people.

Vladimir Putin’s forces launched 28 missiles in a 20-minute nightmare blitzkrieg sparking over an hour of air raid alerts.

The attack is one of the deadliest strikes on Kyiv this year.



President Volodymyr Zelensky said the night of attacks resulted in “horrific casualties and destruction”.

News.title: Tragedy as boy swept out to sea while playing with pals ‘just 11 minutes’ after lifeguards clocked off before body found
News.content:
A TEENAGE boy has died after he was swept out to sea while playing with his friends just 11 minutes after the lifeguards clocked off, a witness says.

Emergency services scoured the coast just off Hornsea, East Yorkshire, before the boy’s body was pulled from the water in the early hours of yesterday morning.



HM Coastguard were first on the scene following reports the boy had vanished at 6.11pm, just 11 minutes after the lifeguards had finished up.

The sea was said to be “rough and windy” on Tuesday evening.



A female eyewitness said: “The coastguards came flying down, I remember checking the time because I thought the lifeguards are still here.

“But it was 11 minutes past six and they knock off at six. The lifeguards had only just left. It was only just after they had clocked off unfortunately.



“There were people stood on the wall looking. The coastguards had their binoculars out looking. Then the cavalry arrived – helicopters, ambulances, police and all sorts.

“There were four out in the sea, and three were rescued. I think he must have swept this way because they came further up.



“It was pretty rough seas and windy. The air ambulance landed on a field nearby. I don’t think they were surfing,

“They were just in the sea because they were very young, We saw them when they came up. They were just playing in the sea.

“I don’t think they were around here because they did not appear to know a lot about sea safety. It’s a shame because all season the lifeguards have had a sign up warning people of rip tides.

“They would have been safer if they were on this part of the beach unfortunately. But they could not see the sign from where they were.

“The emergency services were so quick to respond. They just could not see him or find where he was. It is all it takes – a split second.”



Another male eyewitness said: “They shut down the seafront. There were a load of ambulances and the police came down.

“The helicopter was going up and down all night. They sent a coastguard plane down later on.

“The police brought the surviving kids up here eventually. I saw one go away in an ambulance because he was there for quite a while.”

The other two children were reportedly taken away in a police car.

“I did not see any parents. They would probably have come up the Pennine Trail from Hull. It is the closest seaside town to Hull,” he added.



“There is always groups of kids from Hull on their bike. It is a relatively safe journey because you have just got the Trail.”

Two helicopters were involved in the search along with lifeboats from Bridlington and Hornsea.

Enquiries are ongoing to piece together exactly what happened.

Anyone with information that could assist the investigation is asked to contact the police right away.

Chief Superintendent Phil Booker, of Humberside Police, said: “After receiving the report, officers were immediately deployed alongside other emergency services and upon attending, it was discovered that a 13-year-old boy had reportedly got into difficulty whilst swimming in the water.



“Our priority now is to find the boy, and members of the public can expect to see specialist Police Search Advisors (POLSA), along with our Marine Unit and drone pilots, who have also been deployed to conduct an extensive search and rescue operation to locate him.

“We would urge people to please avoid the area where possible to allow emergency services to work efficiently and safely, and refrain from speculating on the circumstances of the incident.

“Our enquiries continue to ascertain the full circumstances around the report, and we would ask anyone with any information that may assist us.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police said any witnesses should contact them via their non-emergency number 101 quoting log 415 of 4 August.

News.title: Nigel Farage promises ‘Deliveroo Law’ and fines if big businesses hire illegal workers
News.content:
NIGEL Farage promised a ‘Deliveroo Law’ and fines of 10 per cent of global turnover if big businesses hire illegal workers.

CEOs could be made liable for illegal migrants in their company even if they claim they did not know staff were in the UK unlawfully.



Reform will use cash taken from firms who employ workers unlawfully and give it to the victims of migrant crime and schemes to revive struggling high streets.

Mr Farage pledged to launch a Turkish Barber tip line, encouraging the public and companies to report suspected illicit working on Britain’s high streets.



Police forces will be mandated to follow up every tip.

Reform UK Home Affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said the Tories and Labour made Britain the softest-touch country in the world for illegal migrants to undercut British workers.



He said Reform will offer the “harshest penalties in the world for those employing illegal migrants”.

“There are companies whose entire business model is based on profiting from illegal working. It is a slap in the face to the public.

“It makes a mockery of our immigration laws, takes jobs from British workers and is funding the people smugglers in the Channel.”

Top bosses will be sent to prison for employing illegal migrants under Reform plans.



The party claimed young Brits are being shunned from the workforce due to illegal migrants cutting in.

A Deliveroo spokesperson said: “Illegal working should absolutely be addressed, and that’s why we’ve led the industry in cracking down on the sophisticated, organised criminals who attempt to abuse our platform.

“We run Right to Work checks on all riders, conduct multiple daily identity checks and use cutting-edge fraud-detection technology, and we’d encourage other industries affected by illegal working to do the same.”

A Home Office spokesperson added: “Illegal working undermines honest business, exploits vulnerable individuals and fuels organised immigration crime.

“We are already closing the loopholes that allow illegal migrants to work in the UK by extending right to work checks to the gig economy and delivery sector.



“Employers who break the law face severe consequences, including fines of up to £60,000 per illegal worker, business closures, licence revocations and prison sentences of up to five years.

“Since July 2024, we have increased Immigration Enforcement action to the highest level in British history, with illegal working arrests up by 83% and raids up by 77%.”

News.title: Top Putin commander killed in Moscow restaurant blast is identified after secretive burial as Vlad loses another general
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BASH BLAST Top Putin commander killed in Moscow restaurant blast is identified after secretive burial as Vlad loses another general

A SECRET burial has been held for a top Russian commander killed in a bomb blast at an elite Moscow restaurant, reports say.

The high-security ceremony for Lt-Gen Igor Yerusalimov, 53, took place at Troekurovskoye cemetery.



Yerusalimov was reportedly one of five killed in the attack that targeted the lavish party of the notorious Col-Gen Alexander Chayko on Saturday.

High-ranking military officers, politicians and top bureaucrats had gathered inside the exclusive Balzi Rossi, overlooking Moscow’s Kudrinskaya Squarewhen, when the home-made device detonated.



Yerusalimov was at the front of the restaurant as a female courier was stopped by a security operative as she carried a “gift” for Chayko.

The birthday present exploded killing the woman carrying the bomb, a security officer and three others.

Another 21 attendees are reportedly in a serious condition, some with their limbs blown off.

The Kremlin tried to hide the names of victims killed in the suspected Ukrainian special services operation.



Chayko – a decorated Hero of Russia who turned 55 last week – was the commander of Russian forces on the Kyiv front during the Bucha Massacre.

His troops committed barbaric mass rapes and tortures in what is seen as one of the worst Russian crimes of the conflict.

Ukraine designated him a wanted “war criminal” over his alleged role in the 2022 horrors.

Now in charge of Vladimir Putin’s air-based nuclear forces, the general was reportedly not among the wounded.

But his daughter Maria, 25, was seriously wounded, suffering a “traumatic brain injury”, according to sources.



Her husband Daniil Peredriy, 27, was also killed in the blast.

The woman carrying the gift was likely used as a “suicide bomber” without her knowledge, a source told Kommersant.

Police and paramedics rushed to the Stalin-era high-rise building hosting the restaurant on Kudrinskaya Square in central Moscow.



It comes as another senior Russian commander was reportedly killed by a Ukrainian FPV drone.

Major General Dmitry Mikhailov, 39, one of Putin’s youngest generals, is said to have suffered fatal injuries while travelling in an armoured Tigr vehicle.

He had allegedly ignored repeated warnings about the threat posed by Ukrainian drones before entering the combat zone.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mikhailov has also been accused of war crimes during Russia‘s occupation of the Izium region, with Ukrainian investigators naming him among those responsible.

More than a dozen Russian generals have been killed since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

News.title: Andy Burnham is picking the wrong fight by refusing to block PC Harper killers’ release
News.content:
Force his hand

DOES Andy Burnham really want a damaging court battle with the appalled police colleagues of an officer brutally killed in the line of duty?

His decision not to block the release of two of PC Andrew Harper’s killers has spectacularly backfired.



Remorseless thugs Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole laughed in the faces of Andrew’s grieving family at their trial.

They are the worst kind of scum and represent a huge risk to public safety.



That’s why more than 400,000 people have signed a petition calling for them to stay behind bars.

It’s also why the Chief Constable of Thames Valley Police says he is considering joining a Police Federation legal challenge against Burnham’s ruling.

Does our new Prime Minister really want to find himself in a Judicial Review, brought by the coppers he relies on to keep voters safe?

Is he sure he wants to spend taxpayer money defending his position in such a legal battle?

Not only would it be morally wrong, but it would also be politically stupid for Burnham to effectively line up on the side of two cop-killers.

There is already legislation in Andrew’s name — Harper’s Law — which recognises assaulting an emergency services worker is an aggravating factor.



Extending this principle to the manslaughter of a cop — and excluding anybody guilty of this heinous crime from the early release scheme — is one way out of this mess.

Burnham knows MPs of all parties would back emergency legislation to keep Bowers and Cole locked up.

The public mood on this is clear.

Just do the right thing, PM.

Police support

IN another shameful case of police being let down, why did it take so long for the brave gun cop at the centre of the Chris Kaba shooting to finally be cleared?



In 2024, Sgt Martyn Blake was acquitted of murder after the death of gangster Kaba at a road block two years earlier.

But under pressure from Kaba’s family, the Independent Office for Police Conduct probed Sgt Blake for misconduct for another two years.

Met Police Commissioner Sir Mark Rowley is right to describe the hounding of Sgt Blake as a disgrace.

Armed officers risking their lives in the line of duty deserve protection — not endless investigation.

Neet again

AT 16, young people should expect to have a world of opportunity ahead of them.



But for a huge number, it marks the age in which they are sucked into the welfare doom loop.

The Sun reveals today a staggering 65 per cent of 16-year-olds not in work, education or training remain so a year later.

It’s a quagmire of hopelessness from which too many never emerge.

News.title: PC Andrew Harper’s devastated widow tells Burnham ‘you should be ashamed’ as she slams killers’ planned early release
News.content:
THE widow of hero PC Andrew Harper described the planned early release of two of his killers as a “punch in the gut” — and told PM Andy Burnham: “You should be ashamed.”

Devastated Lissie Harper said she will “never give up” in her bid to have Albert Bowers and Jessie Cole exempted from a scheme to let out prisoners guilty of manslaughter halfway through their sentence.



And she has thrown her weight behind an online Thames Valley Police Federation petition to stop his killers being freed, which more than 400,000 people had signed on Wednesday evening.

The Federation is also taking legal action over their early release — a move the chief constable of PC Harper’s force confirmed that he was considering joining.



A poll for The Sun, meanwhile, revealed that 94 per cent of our readers want Andy Burnham to block the release of the two killers.

PC Harper died while investigating the theft of a £10,000 quad bike near Sulhamstead, Berks, in August 2019.



Bowers and Cole, then 17, tried to escape in a car driven by Henry Long, 18.

The 28-year-old officer’s ankles got caught in a heavy-duty tow strap and he suffered ­catastrophic ­injuries as he was dragged in the dark for more than a mile at an average 43mph.

Bowers and Cole were sentenced to 13 years in July 2020, meaning they could be released by October.

Long, the main perpetrator, who pleaded guilty, got 16 years and is not eligible for release under the scheme.



Lissie, who had married PC Harper just four weeks before the tragedy, said: “Hopefully we can make the current Government come to their senses and realise we cannot put people like this back on our streets.

“Justice should mean justice and serving the sentence given.

“The Government has punched us in the gut . . . they should be ashamed of themselves.”



She urged the public to put their names to the Police Federation’s ­petition, which is getting around 12,500 signatures an hour.

It is quadruple the 100,000 mark, the point at which petitions are considered for debate in Parliament.

Lissie, of Wallingford, Oxfordshire, said: “Please sign our petition . . . we will never give up.”

The Thames Valley Police Chief Constable Jason Hogg said he was receiving legal advice on whether the force could join the challenge.

He said: “This is something I ­certainly would consider.



“I do think that the public opinion is overwhelming in this matter.

“I think it’s unfair and I do believe confidence in the criminal justice ­system risks being damaged.

“It’s right for the Government to have a look at this.”

He said it was “perverse” that ­Bowers and Cole were eligible for release and said the knowledge they were has had a “profound” effect on his 10,000 officers and staff.

He said he was “beyond disappointed” the Government was allowing Cole and Bowers to walk free early.



Chief Constable Hogg stressed there was a loophole in the justice system.

He said Harper’s Law, for which Lissie fought and which is named for PC Harper, means anyone convicted of the manslaughter of an on-duty emergency worker gets a mandatory life term.

He said that would be Cole and Bowers’ fate if convicted.



He has written to Andy Burnham demanding emergency legislation to close the loophole which enables the pair to be freed.

Aileen O’Connor, who chairs the Thames Valley Police Federation, said letting the two out would anger and demoralise serving officers.

She said: “I will throw everything I can at this through a proper legal challenge. Our colleagues will accept nothing less. It is a final betrayal from the politicians.”

She thanked all those who have signed the petition, adding: “I couldn’t believe in my wildest dreams that we would have reached that amount of ­signatures in such a short space of time.

“The Government need to listen and to be on the right side of this” Tory leader Kemi Badenoch said she supported the Federation.



She said: “I’m not arguing against early release. We’ve had early release even under Conservatives.

“I’m against early release of this dangerous category of rapists, ­paedophiles, killers, including the killers of PC Andrew Harper.”

She told The Sun: “It doesn’t have to be like this. In 14 years of Conservative government we never let rapists, paedophiles and killers out early.

“In fact, we made sure any early release was after two-thirds of a ­sentence. Labour have now lowered that to just one third.”



PM Mr Burnham, currently on his summer holiday, is facing mounting pressure to exclude the killers of emergency workers as part of the initiative to free up prison spaces.

Some 5,000 criminals will be released over ten months from October. After the Government re-considered the scheme those convicted of rape, ­serious child sexual offences and grooming will be excluded.

However, justice minister Jake ­Richards confirmed Bowers and Cole would remain subject to early release.

He argued: “It would be wrong to pick out individual cases within different offending cohorts.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“That wouldn’t be right. It wouldn’t be lawful either. I understand the strength of feeling from police ­officers generally, but of course within that force in particular after the awful incident with PC Harper.

“If we do not have prison places available then the police, the good work that they do every day on the streets, finding perpetrators, locking them up, it would be impossible.”

News.title: Teen dressed as clown ‘stabbed elderly man to death’ after whispering horrifying message to doorbell cam
News.content:
A TEEN who dressed as a clown and whispered sinister messages into a Ring doorbell has been accused of the murder of a pensioner.

The 15-year-old boy was taken into custody after John Wesley Allen Sr, 76, was stabbed several times in Illinois.



Cops were called to a residential street in East St. Louis around 10pm on Monday, August 3, following reports of a body lying near or in the roadway.

The body was identified as that of Allen and a coroner ruled he had died from multiple stab wounds.



The 15-year-old suspect was taken into custody by the Illinois State Police on Tuesday afternoon in connection with Allen’s death.

It has now been revealed the teenager was spotted earlier on Monday in the area dressed as a clown.

Ring doorbell footage posted to social media, with a timestamp of around 9pm – just an hour before the cops were called – shows a person dressed as a clown at a home in East St. Louis.

The clown leaves the audio message: “I’ve been looking for you.”



Lee Palmer told First Alert 4 that his mother was at the home alone when the clown appeared on their front porch.

He said the person lingered on the property for several minutes and even went behind the house.

Palmer said he was worried the clown was going to “kill everyone in the house.”

He said: “I couldn’t believe it.

“He was dressed in the clown outfit



“That was kind of spooky for her.”

Palmer also worried the teen was armed.

Illinois State Police say they arrested a 15-year-old suspect who they believe to have been seen on surveillance video wearing a clown costume.

They have not released details about what led to the killing or what brought the teen to the neighbourhood.

They said: “Video footage of the suspect dressed in a clown costume has been circulating and ISP is currently working to collect all relevant video.”



Investigators are urging anyone with information or surveillance video of the clown-clad suspect to contact them.

It comes as a blood-covered clown lied to cops after he battered a male model to death at a party.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Bhekisani Matabiswana, 27, punched, kicked and stamped on 37-year-old Luke Harden until he died.

He told cops at the scene he had discovered Luke suffering a cardiac arrest on a road close to the party in Lancashire.

News.title: Labour accused of giving Jeffrey Epstein victims false hope after public inquiry ruled out
News.content:
JEFFREY Epstein’s victims were given false hope that Labour was considering a public inquiry into his UK activities, the Tories say.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham was said to be looking into a full-scale probe by junior minister Alex Davies-Jones.



But the Government distanced itself from her comments within hours, insisting an inquiry was not being actively considered.

The Conservatives’ Deputy Chairman Matt Vickers accused Labour of “freelancing on the airwaves”.



He told The Sun: “You cannot run a Government on a whim, especially when the issues are this serious.”

His comments came after Victims Minister Ms Davies-Jones told BBC’s Newsnight the Government was reviewing “what is possible” and had been assured the PM is “taking this very seriously”.



She added: “He will meet with those victims and he is looking at what is possible, now he has access to all of the information as Prime Minister to see what action we can take.”

The suggestion Labour was set to hold an inquiry had been positively received by campaign groups.



Ms Davies-Jones accused Mr Burnham’s predecessor Sir Keir Starmer of failing to listen to Epstein’s victims.

Campaigners have also called for a probe into alleged sexual misconduct by Harrods owner Mohamed Fayed, who died in 2023.

News.title: Covent Garden stabbing live: Police arrest woman in London as four men attacked
News.content:
A woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed with a weapon believed to be a pair of scissors in Covent Garden, central London

A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in what police think was an "isolated mental health-related incident" in central London.

The woman has been held on suspicion of possessing an offensive weapon – believed to be a pair of scissors – and assault after the Wednesday lunchtime incident in busy Covent Garden, an area filled with bars, theatres and restaurants.

Two men are being treated in hospital for injuries which are not life-threatening or life-changing and the other two were discharged.

They are aged 34, 39, 42 and 52. The woman was held by officers from the Metropolitan Police's Parliamentary and Diplomatic Protection unit, who happened to be in the area at the time of the attack.

Members of the elite armed police unit drew their Tasers during the incident. The highly trained officers normally protect high-profile individuals and sites of national importance.

News.title: Elderly woman fed dog food by care workers before death in 'litany of errors'
News.content:
Elderly woman fed dog food by care workers before death in 'litany of errors'

An investigation was opened after concerns were raised by the woman's family as she was left alone for 'prolonged periods' with 'inconsistent' care in the months leading up to her death

View 3 Images The woman was fed dog food in her final months (stock image) (Image: Getty Images)

A woman was fed dog food by care workers months before her death as they made a 'litany of errors'.

‌



Portsmouth City Council have apologised for the incident, after care workers employed by Radis, who were contracted to provide home care for the council did not provide 'sufficient' care for the elderly lady.

‌



It has been determined that the care she received amounted to a “significant personal injustice” following a report by the Local Government and Social Care Ombudsman.

‌



View 3 Images An investigation was opened into the care the woman received (stock image) (Image: Getty)

The woman, referred to as Mrs Y, received at-home care from GP Homecare Ltd, known as Radis.

Her care, after she was left with reduced mobility and confined to her bed following a fall in April 2024, raised concerns from her family.

‌



She was often left for prolonged periods of time, with her son noting a “lack of management oversight at Radis”.

He said staff did not refer to her care plan, visits were not recorded accurately and a ‘Do Not Attempt Resuscitation’ document was found “scrunched up in a cupboard”.

Following these complaints, a Section 42 safeguarding enquiry was opened by the council, with Radis also launching an internal investigation.

‌



In this period, Mrs Y suffered a mini-stroke and it was agreed she needed a “soft diet due to the increased risk of choking”.

But, in mid-June 2024, a care worker was caught feeding her dog food, recorded as a “lamb dinner”.

The incident occurred when two care workers attended Mrs Y's home, with one raising concerns about witnessing this error.

‌



The care worker “only realised the meat was dog food when they noticed the packaging in the kitchen”.

They initially attempted to contact a senior colleague to report the issue but their call was not answered so they waited and reported the incident in person the following week.

When they did so, a senior manager asked “why they did not remove the dog food” during the visit and “why they did not report the incident on the day it happened”.

‌



The care worker was also told to remove the dog food from Mrs Y’s freezer “to prevent any other care workers doing the same”.

View 3 Images The woman was fed food meant for dogs (Image: Grace Cary / Getty Images)

It was later revealed that the care worker “fed three mouthfuls of microwaved dog food to Mrs Y”.

‌



"This was vacuum packed dog food stored by Mrs Z in Mrs Y’s freezer. The food was labelled as “fresh take on dog food” and “for adult dogs and puppies”.”

After this, a meeting between Radis and the family, concluded a new care provider would be hired.

However, in July 2024, Mrs Y's health declined and her family decided to delay the new provider's start date, meaning Radis continued to provide end-of-life care.

‌



Mrs Y’s daughter alleged that “footage from Mrs Y’s home camera showed evidence of a care worker force feeding Mrs Y”.

In late July 2024, Mrs Y died and it was concluded she “died from frailty of old age”.

In response to complaint's from the elderly woman's family Radis accepted fault in the care provided and ensured action was taken against the care workers involved.

‌



The council's investigation also found that Mrs Y was “left unattended for prolonged periods and on occasions left wet or in darkness overnight”

The report stated that staffing was “inconsistent”, with concerns raised about workers “attitude, compassion and respectful communication”.

There were also “Allegations that staff falsified records and that some visits had not taken place despite being recorded”.

‌



The ombudsman proposed the council apologise, refund the care fees, and offer a symbolic payment of £1,000 to the family to “recognise significant distress” and the “delays” in the safeguarding investigation.

Councillor Matthew Winnington, cabinet member for community wellbeing, health and care, said: “We accept the Ombudsman’s findings in full and recognise the seriousness of what happened in this case. We ended our contract with Radis early and we no longer work with, or commission services from them.

“The care described in this report is not the standard anyone should expect, particularly at such a vulnerable time in someone’s life. We have apologised to the family and are very sorry for the distress they have experienced; we know this has been deeply upsetting for the family.

Article continues below

He added: “These events happened two years ago, and since then we have taken action to strengthen how we oversee care providers...Our adult social care services recently received a ‘good’ rating from the Care Quality Commission, reflecting the wider positive experiences of residents, the strength of partnership working across the city, and the support available to help people remain independent."

News.title: Iran deal to open Strait of Hormuz in 'final stage' after Trump 'demands answers' over missile stockpiles
News.content:
Iran deal to open Strait of Hormuz in 'final stage' after Trump 'demands answers' over missile stockpiles

The US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian sites on February 28 and Iran retaliated by striking sites across the Middle East and closing the strait

View 3 Images (L/R) US Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, President Donald Trump and Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth attend a Cabinet meeting at Camp David in Maryland, on July 31, 2026 (Image: Getty Images)

Iran has said that it is in the "final stage" of drafting an agreement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, which could see the waterway reopens for commercial shipping. The statement comes after US President Donald Trump has said a deal could be announced this week.

‌



The critical waterway has been a contentious issue in the US-Iran war. The US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian sites on February 28 and Iran retaliated by striking sites across the Middle East and closing the strait.

‌



But the agreement is likely to be contingent on the US lifting its blockade on Iran's ports. The Trump administration has previously ruled out any deal that would cement Iran's grip over the strait, which would amount to a major loss for the US and a break with global norms.

‌



View 3 Images Three boys play in the shallow waters of the Strait of Hormuz, as a plume of smoke rises from an explosion in the background, off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Monday, July 13, 2026 (Image: AP Photo/Razieh Poudat)

Iran has insisted on some measure of control over the strait, saying it will not go back to being an open international waterway, as it was before the war.

The ability for the US to continue the conflict has been thrown into the spotlight after reports that tensions rose between the president and his head of war over American levels of munition.

‌



A furious Mr Trump reportedly demanded answers from Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth over extreme munitions shortages, according to the Washington Post.

The paper reports that an exchange at the Camp David summit over the weekend underscored the president's "increasing frustration with Mr Hegseth," who was one of the biggest early advocates for taking military action against Iran.

Mr Trump is said to have "demanded answers" from Mr Hegseth on why he had apparently been misled on extreme munitions shortages that now threaten to limit military options with Iran, two people familiar with the exchange told The Washington Post.

‌



View 3 Images US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth looks on as US President Donald Trump speaks after signing an executive order establishing the President's Military Spouse Commission in the Oval Office at the White House on August 03, 2026 (Image: Getty)

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt has hit back at the report, claimiung it the exchange did not take place and branding it "fake news".

She said in a post on X: "I was at Camp David with President Trump and Secretary Hegseth.

‌



"This literally never happened, and we told the Washington Post that repeatedly.

"This B.S. story was shopped to many outlets by someone clearly out to disparage the Secretary, for whatever reason.

"Unfortunately for them, the President loves the Secretary and thinks he's doing a tremendous job.

Article continues below

"FAKE NEWS!"

News.title: Major UK school uniform rule change to take place from September 2026
News.content:
Major UK school uniform rule change to take place from September 2026

A major UK school uniform change is in place from September this year as the government attempts to save parents with school-aged children more money each year

View 2 Images The major school uniform change starts next month [stock image] (Image: Tesco)

From September, schools across the UK have to follow a strict new uniform rule that has been implemented in an attempt to save parents money.

‌



Starting next month at the beginning of the new school year, most schools will only be permitted to ask parents/carers to buy a maximum of three branded uniform items per child.

‌



The change has been made by the government in order to make school uniforms more affordable.

‌



View 2 Images The new rules are a bid to save parents money (Image: Getty Images)

School uniforms are a hefty expense, with the average cost for primary school pupils totally £350 and £442 for secondary students, although this can massively differ based on what different schools require.

The new rules are applicable to academy schools and trusts, maintained schools, non-maintained special schools, pupil referral units and local authorities.

‌



The new guidelines state that all branded items should be kept to a minimum.

This means that from September 2026:

schools must limit the number of compulsory branded items of uniform and PE kit to three or fewer

secondary and middle schools must limit the number of compulsory branded items of uniform and PE kit to four or fewer, if one is a tie

‌



The government website also states that 'schools should ensure that their uniform supply arrangements give the highest priority to cost and value for money' in order to stop parents having to make several repurchases.

Despite these changes being part of the Education (Guidance about Costs of School Uniforms) Act 2021 a survey of 1,000 parents with school-aged children found that 48% had no idea of the new rules, according to advice site Money Wellness.

Even though the plan is in place to help cut costs parents remain divide over how much of a difference they will make.

Article continues below

Around three in five (61%) think limiting branded items will save them money, but 30% are not expecting to see any saving at all.

News.title: Hero who tried to stop thieves dies after beating from kids as young as 12
News.content:
Hero who tried to stop thieves dies after beating from kids as young as 12

Grocery shop owner Van Viet Truong tried to step in and help a fellow retail worker when a scuffle broke out - he has since died after suffering a strike to the head

View 5 Images CCTV footage shows Van Viet Truong as he tried to intervene as a nearby shop was being robbed by a gang of kids

A man has died after being allegedly bashed by a group of children as young as 12 after they fled from a shop with allegedly stolen goods. Grocery shop owner Van Viet Truong, 60, stepped in to help a fellow retail worker who was being robbed in Melbourne, Australia, when he was set upon by the gang of youths. He made chase when the drama unfolded last week, and was coming to the aid of a nearby employee at a shop on Hampshire Road just after 2pm when a scuffle broke out in the street. Truong appears to push one of the children before he is struck in the head. As per CCTV footage from the incident, what happened next occurred out of the view of security cameras.

View 5 Images A man has died after being bashed by this group of children, police say

But, as per Victoria Police, the shopkeeper was left with significant head injuries after he was allegedly struck in the head a number of times and hit his head on the ground.

Truong was transported to hospital where he sadly died on Wednesday afternoon. Three boys aged 12, 13 and 15 years old from the Brimbank area, a 14-year-old girl from the Banyule area and a 14-year-old girl from the Brimbank area have each since been charged with affray, violent disorder, intentionally cause serious injury and intentionally cause injury. They were remanded to appear before a children’s court at a later date. Further investigations exonerated the 13-year-old boy, and his charges have since been withdrawn by police. However, in the wake of Truong's death, Detectives from Victoria Police are now considering upgrading the charges against the children.

View 5 Images Melbourne hero Van Viet Truong - who tried to stop robbery in Sunshine - has died

Magistrate Robyn Hamilton foreshadowed the 60-year-old grocery shop owner's death, saying he had been “left in an unsurvivable situation, and it’s inevitable the charges of affray and intentionally causing serious injury will be upgraded”. “Within days or hours, that victim will die, that was the grim message from a magistrate at a children’s court,” she said. Magistrate Hamilton added the alleged actions of the children had “resulted in the worst possible outcome”. As per news.com.au, one mum entered a plea to the court on Sunday through tears, begging for her 12-year-old son to be granted bail. She expressed fears for his mental health and physical safety, but was ultimately unsuccessful. Several of the teens are expected to face the court again later this week to have their bail examined.

View 5 Images He is understood to have two small children of his own

Talkback host Jacqui Felgate fumed on Monday on her 3AW radio programme that the horror incident should be making front page headlines, but it had fallen by the wayside due to a wider issue with children and crime in the city that has been normalised. “We have allowed children to think that this is OK. That actions don’t have consequences and that if you commit a crime you don’t go to jail,” she said.

Article continues below

“And this happened because the government reacted many years ago to a death in custody and weakened bail laws. It should never have happened, but this is the unintended consequences.

View 5 Images CCTV footage shows Van Viet Truong as he tried to intervene as a nearby shop was being robbed by a gang of kids

“For years, youth offenders and children don’t go to jail. They get bail and they know it. For (the government) to say we have the toughest bail laws in the country, these children ... they laugh at police.” Victorian state Premier Ben Carroll has since labelled the alleged attack on the 60-year-old man as “completely unacceptable”. “This is terrible what occurred to this gentleman, there’s no tolerance for this sort of behaviour. It’s awful … it’s completely unacceptable,” Mr Carroll said. He conceded the case should be subject to the state of Victoria’s ‘adult time for violent crime’ initiative.

News.title: Horror as sleepwalking mum plunges 40ft from balcony on holiday
News.content:
Horror as sleepwalking mum plunges 40ft from balcony on holiday

Raina Heverin, 44, fell two storeys into a courtyard after opening a window beside a Juliet balcony while sleepwalking. She suffered a bleed on the brain, a punctured lung, a broken hip, arm and ribs and spent three weeks in a coma

View 4 Images Raina Heverin was left with a life-changing brain injury after plunging 40ft from a balcony while sleepwalking on holiday (Image: Raina Heverin / SWNS)

A mum-of-two was left with a life-changing brain injury after plunging 40ft from a balcony while sleepwalking on holiday in Paris.

‌



The horror unfolded on April 26 last year after Raina Heverin, 44, swapped bedrooms with her brother and sister-in-law at the townhouse where they were staying. She had complained that traffic outside her room at the front of the property had kept her awake. The couple offered her their quieter bedroom at the back, which had a Juliet balcony.

‌



Raina, from Liverpool, Merseyside, went to the room after a day sightseeing but remembers nothing about the fall - and believes she was sleepwalking. At 6am, her brother noticed the bedroom door was open and initially assumed she had gone for a morning run. But her shoes were still inside and the window was open.

‌



View 4 Images Raina Heverin in recovery. (Image: Raina Heverin / SWNS)

Lightning strikes football pitch killing player and injuring 12 others READ MORE :

When he looked down, he saw Raina lying motionless in the courtyard below. She said: "My brother and sister-in-law were in disbelief. It was really horrible for them."

The couple did not speak French, but a neighbour helped them call an ambulance.

‌



Raina was rushed to hospital with devastating injuries and remained unconscious for three weeks. She suffered a bleed on the brain, a punctured lung, a broken hip, arm and ribs and spent three weeks in a coma.

Raina said: "I was in Paris for a long weekend with my brother and sister-in-law. We had spent the day walking around Paris - it was awesome, we had food and went everywhere. We went went back to the apartment at about midnight - but I don't remember anything after that."

She said: "I had a broken arm and a big scar down my arm, I broke my hip, I punctured my lung, I had lots of broken ribs. If I had been found a few hours later, I definitely wouldn't be here."

‌



View 4 Images Raina Heverin in hospital. (Image: Raina Heverin / SWNS)

Before the accident, Raina was an active mum who ran two businesses while raising Cian, 10, and Aliyah, eight. She exercised every day and regularly ran 10km, cycled, lifted weights and attended fitness classes.

A doctor in France later told her family that her physical fitness had helped save her life. Raina spent two months in hospital in France before returning to Britain. She then spent a week at Whiston Hospital and five months at Broadgreen Hospital before moving into a specialist brain injury rehabilitation unit in November.

‌



Raina was diagnosed with ataxia, a neurological condition which affects balance, coordination and muscle movement. She also suffered a bleed on the brain and polytrauma - multiple traumatic injuries affecting different areas and systems of the body.

She now struggles to balance and suffers tremors in her hands, body and throat. Raina said: "It's hard for me to do normal things - like putting on mascara or holding a cup of coffee. Putting make-up on takes a lot longer. I had to re-learn how to do everything."

View 4 Images Raina Heverin with son Cain Heverin,daughter Aliyah Heverin, and husband Michael Heverin (Image: Raina Heverin / SWNS)

‌



Her first memories after waking from the coma are of her husband Michael sitting beside her and reading aloud. She said: "I remember a bit, but I was very disoriented. I didn't know what the hell had happened."

She added: "I think I'm still grieving my old life. I go through periods of being happy and sad at the same time. I feel lucky and unlucky. I still feel like I'm in 2025, but it is a year and four months later. The world has kept turning while I've been in hospital."

Raina has now written a children's book to help Cian and Aliyah understand her brain injury and why their mum has changed. She has also raised more than £4,000 for Liverpool-based The Brain Charity by completing a 5km walking challenge.

Article continues below

Raina walked 40 laps of her garden over four days, supported by friends and relatives while her children held up a banner. She said: "It feels like a massive achievement. I'm excited for the future, because I know it can only get better."

When asked what she would say to other people in rehabilitation, Raina said: "Don't give up, keep going. You're going to have some bad days, but you're going to have good days too. There's a life that's worth living."

News.title: Donald Trump in 'safety incident' between Marine One and passenger jet
News.content:
Donald Trump in 'safety incident' between Marine One and passenger jet

Investigations are underway into what happened when a commercial jet took off just as the president's helicopter left the White House with Donald Trump on board

View 3 Images US President Donald Trump walks over to Marine One after landing in Air Force One on July 03, 2026 at Ellsworth Air Force Base, South Dakota (Image: Getty)

Investigations are underway into why a passenger jet was allowed to take off as US President Donald Trump's helicopter approached.

‌



Marine One was approaching Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on the afternoon of Tuesday, August 4 when the incident occurred - an apparent violation of safety procedures put in place after last year's mid-air collision near the busy airport.

‌



Both the National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration said on Wednesday they were investigating what happened when the jet took off just as the helicopter left the White House with the president aboard.

‌



View 3 Images US President Donald Trump steps off Marine One before boarding Air Force One for a trip to Michigan on July 27, 2026 (Image: Getty)

The FAA decided after 67 people died on January 29, 2025, when an airliner collided with an Army Black Hawk helicopter that all take-offs and landings at the Washington, DC airport would be halted anytime a helicopter passes by on a conflicting route.

The airspace near the White House and Reagan is heavily congested with military and commercial aircraft.

‌



The airplane that took off Tuesday was climbing above Marine One as the helicopter approached, so the two aircraft were not on a collision course.

The FAA said in a statement that a preliminary investigation showed "there was a momentary loss of separation after which the aircraft continued to move away from one another."

"The air traffic controller was in contact with both the commercial pilot and Marine One pilot during the loss of separation," the FAA said.

‌



View 3 Images A flock of geese walk on the Ellipse in front of the Washington Monument as Marine One arrives to transfer US President Donald Trump to Joint Base Andrews on July 22, 2026 (Image: Getty)

The White House emphasised that Trump was never in danger.

"Marine One flights are piloted by some of the best aviators in the world, and at no point was the President in harm’s way," White House spokesperson Kush Desai said in a statement.

Article continues below

The Marine Corps defended the actions of their helicopter pilots.

Poor communication between the military and the civilian air traffic controllers at Reagan has been an issue in the past.

News.title: Lightning strikes football pitch killing player and injuring 12 others
News.content:
Lightning strikes football pitch killing player and injuring 12 others

A 24-year-old footballer was tragically killed and 12 others were injured at the Santiphap Stadium in Narathiwat province when a freak lightning strike hit the rain-soaked pitch

View 3 Images Safwan Awae was killed after the lightning strike (Image: Viral Press)

A 24-year-old has sadly died in a freak lightning strike while on the pitch at a football match.

‌



The horror lightning strike happened on Tuesday at Santiphap Stadium in Sungai Golok, with the rival Thai and Malaysian teams facing off in the Golo FA Cup 2026 semi-final in Thailand. Emergency medical services rushed him to a local hospital, but he succumbed to his critical injuries.

‌



A horrifying social media video captured the moment two soccer teams were playing a raucous match in the rain when lightning struck the field in a huge explosion.

‌



View 3 Images The two teams were battling through a fierce monsoon at the Santiphap Stadium in Narathiwat province when the electrical flash tore from the heavens (Image: Viral Press)

Australian woman charged with murder after allegedly starving man with Down's Syndrome to death READ MORE :

The rest of the footage then shows 24-year-old Sofwan Awae in a black-and-white striped jersey, lying face down on the ground before his teammate runs toward him and turns him over. Multiple people, identified as staff members and fellow players, ran towards Awae.

‌



“Although the emergency medical team made every effort to save him, the victim succumbed to severe injuries sustained in the incident,” said Sungai Golok police chief Thun Sirikhunt, as cited by Bernama.

View 3 Images Awae was a winger for SAMCOLTS (Image: Viral Press)

“Although the emergency medical team made every effort to save him, the victim succumbed to severe injuries sustained in the incident,” said Sungai Golok police chief Thun Sirikhunt, according to local media reports.

Article continues below

Several players collapsed to the ground from the strike, and 12 players were injured, Mirror US reports.

Awae was a winger for SAMCOLTS and had reportedly recently signed with Thai third-division club Yala FC.

Among those injured was 22-year-old Malaysian footballer Alif Ezzahan Zulkifli, who was taken to the hospital for treatment.

News.title: Young women tell BBC of rape, assault and harassment at Army training college for teenagers
News.content:
Warning: This article contains sexual language and details of sexual assault

Four young women have told the BBC they were sexually assaulted and harassed at an army training college for teenagers - with one saying she was raped by several fellow junior soldiers in an attack that lasted hours.

The women all attended the Army Foundation College (AFC) at Harrogate, North Yorkshire, over the past five years and say the incidents happened when they were aged 17.

The college has a dangerous culture of misogyny and sexual violence, say the women, who are all speaking out for the first time.

These reports are "extremely distressing and serious", said an Army spokesperson in a statement.

The BBC can also reveal that North Yorkshire Police received 16 reports of sexual offences linked to the college in the year to June, according to a Freedom of Information request.

Those reported offences include allegations of exposure, voyeurism and sexual assault. No information was provided as to whether they had led to prosecutions.

A total of 176 complaints of inappropriate sexual behaviour at the college were made between January 2018 and June 2025, according to Ministry of Defence (MoD) data.

Thirty-two allegations were against permanent staff and 144 against junior soldiers.

"Unacceptable and criminal behaviour has absolutely no place in our Armed Forces," said the Army spokesperson.

"People join in the hope of having a fantastic career and any such reports are unacceptable and go completely against everything the Army stands for."

AFC is the largest military training establishment for under-19s in the UK and it receives all the Army's 16-year-old recruits. There are currently 70 female junior soldiers at the Harrogate site out of a total of 889.

We have changed all the women's names to protect their identities.

News.title: University of Cambridge professor at centre of plagiarism row resigns
News.content:
The University of Cambridge professor at the centre of a plagiarism row has resigned "with immediate effect".

Prof Jason Arday said he had "concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away".

Earlier, the university said it had launched an investigation "following new information" about Arday's "academic qualifications and honorary appointments".

It comes after another academic - self-defined "race realist" Nathan Cofnas, who was sacked from his Cambridge role in 2024 - said he found numerous instances of plagiarism in Arday's work and questioned some of his stated achievements. The academic has admitted errors in his work, but has insisted he is not "a liar".

In a statement posted by the Good Law Project on Wednesday, Arday said that being appointed professor had been "without question, the greatest professional privilege of my life".

"The years since my appointment have also been marked by an unrelenting level of public scrutiny and personal attack," he said, adding "there comes a point when the personal cost becomes too great".

He said his resignation should not "be interpreted as a loss of faith in scholarship or in the values that first brought me to Cambridge.

"Nor should it be mistaken for an acceptance of the narratives that have surrounded me."

Thanking his students and colleagues, he said that "for my own wellbeing, for my family, and for those who have stood by me throughout this difficult period, I have concluded that the only way to bring this chapter to an end is to step away".

Arday said "this is not the end of my work" and that he needed "time to heal".

"When that time comes, I will return," he added.

Earlier on Wednesday, the university said its inquiry had begun "following new information" about Arday's "academic qualifications and honorary appointments".

"Separately, there remains a number of ongoing complaints regarding academic misconduct, which are being handled in line with our Misconduct in Research policy," the University of Cambridge said in a statement.

It added: "While we are fully aware of the public commentary and concerns around this matter, it remains vital that any process is thorough and adheres to both university policies and employment law.

"We also fully recognise that there is a person at the centre of this situation, and we continue to provide support to him."

Jesus College, where Arday is a fellow, has said it is launching its own process "parallel" to the university's investigation.

Jovan Owusu-Nepaul, who describes himself as an associate of Arday, told BBC Newsnight on Wednesday that he found "the whole thing regrettable".

"From, I think, how he's been treated and the quite obtuse spotlight on him about his CV - career - at Cambridge University," he said. "I think it's also regrettable that there may be some untruths that have come out about his CV."

He said it was "appropriate" to respect Arday's request for "a bit of space".

In 2023, the then 37-year-old sociologist became the youngest ever black professor at Cambridge.

Accusations of plagiarism in Arday's work were first voiced by Cofnas - a US researcher whose role at a Cambridge college was terminated after backlash to his view that under a true meritocracy black people would "disappear from almost all high-profile positions outside of sports and entertainment".

He claimed on Substack that he had put Arday's work through a plagiarism detection software, which found that "many passages are lifted with minimal editing, sometimes retaining copy-editing mistakes from the original source".

On Saturday, Arday told the Times in an interview that he was accountable for those mistakes, but that "what I am not is a liar".

He told the newspaper: "There has been, since I arrived at Cambridge, a very well orchestrated and co-ordinated campaign to unseat me from my position."

He suggested that this was "racially motivated" and that he had become a "lightning rod" for criticism of diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) policy.

Arday said some errors in his early academic work was because of his autism, as he relied on using mimicry to make sense of information, and that similar scrutiny would find similar errors in work by other academics.

"We're talking about academia here. I didn't murder somebody. I think the cruelty that I've experienced and the positioning of me as this kind of liar and fantasist is totally unacceptable," he told the newspaper.

Earlier on Wednesday, publisher Simon & Schuster - which is set to publish Arday's memoir later this month - defended Arday in a statement to AFP news agency.

"We are proud to publish Professor Jason Arday. We have worked closely with him... and can speak to the professionalism and integrity he has brought to every stage of the publication," Simon & Schuster said.

News.title: Car washes and vape shops can still sponsor skilled foreign workers despite visa changes
News.content:
More than 1,900 small high street businesses including mini-marts, vape shops and car washes are licensed to sponsor foreign workers under a specialist scheme intended for high-earning individuals despite visa rules being tightened, BBC Verify has found.

The Home Office scheme allows registered employers to recruit workers from overseas who meet a certain skill level. The rules were tightened in July 2025 to restrict the scheme mostly to graduate-level employees who would be earning at least Â£41,700.

But a year on from the rule change, BBC Verify has found more than 1,500 grocery and convenience stores, 150 taxi operators, 100 barber shops, and dozens of car washes and vape shops are still on the register and able to sponsor people to apply for visas.

More than 100 of those businesses were added to the skilled worker sponsorship list after the rules were tightened. Being on the register does not mean applications for individual visas would be approved.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood ordered an urgent review into the presence of vape shops, barbers and car washes on the skilled worker sponsor register two months ago, following concerns over the "potential misuse of the system". The Home Office said at the time that any businesses seeking to abuse the system would have their licences revoked.

A Home Office spokesperson said: "We have raised the skilled worker threshold and over 100 occupations are now ineligible for new skilled worker visas."

It is understood some of the companies that joined the register after the rules changed may have applied before they took effect. Some companies may have also remained on the register because they were approved before July 2025 or are sponsoring workers who were already in the UK.

There are more than 120,000 businesses with licences to sponsor skilled workers. The skilled worker scheme was introduced after Brexit for employers to recruit workers after Eu free movement ended. Smaller firms must pay a Â£611 fee to apply to join the register while larger businesses, such as those with more than 50 staff, pay a fee of Â£1,682. Anyone can be visited by the UK Visas and Immigration service during the application process.

Until July last year, someone being hired from abroad could qualify for sponsorship if their qualifications met an A-Level or equivalent standard, as long as they were paid at least Â£38,700 in most cases. Since the rule change, non-graduate professions, such as shop managers, are no longer eligible to apply. There are also higher English-language skill requirements that were introduced in January this year.

The Home Office said there were 68,067 skilled worker visas granted in the 12 months to March this year - 29,745 to main applicants and 38,322 to their dependants - which is 30% lower than the year before. IT professionals were the most common type of people to be granted the visas, followed by those people working in finance, while the fall in approvals was mostly attributed to those in food preparation and hospitality trades no longer qualifying for the scheme.

News.title: Half of vaccines are binned - 'fridge-free' versions could change that
News.content:
Prof Saul Faust, the director of the NIHR Clinical Research Facility in Southampton, said it gave "equivalent" immune responses to the conventional vaccine as well as being "safe and well tolerated" in the early stage studies.

Faust added: "This obviously has potential to remove cold chain dependence, reduce wastage and improve access."

A larger trial involving 160 people is already due to start in the coming months.

This would be the final stage of research as the original vaccine is already approved and licensed so there is no requirement to perform large-stage trials needed for a novel vaccine.

The studies are being done to meet the World Health Organization's (WHO) goal of a vaccine that survives at 30C and 75% relative humidity.

But the research team say separate data shows the components of their vaccine also survive cycling between temperatures of -20C and +40C. That could mean the vaccine being viable after transport in a cold aircraft hold and then in the back of a truck in the heat.

There is not one single reason vaccines are wasted and disposed of, but the WHO estimates this is the fate of half of all vaccines globally. This can include damage in transport, passing the expiration date, and unused doses from multi-dose vials, but a major factor are failures in the cold chain.

News.title: Why phones on loudspeaker may become just another noise
News.content:
Listen to Angus read the story here

Most days on my commute, I am treated to the contents of strangers' phones.

It could be a teenage boy slouching on a seat on the top deck of the number 29, holding his device inches from his face, either unaware or indifferent that everyone else can hear what he's watching too.

Or a woman taking a phone call on loudspeaker before scrolling at volume through her social feed.

Surveys suggest that many do find this modern phenomenon - known as loudcasting, sodcasting, or headphone dodging - similarly frustrating.

In recent years, Ofcom, YouGov and Transport for London (TfL) have all published polls showing the vast majority of people dislike it. TfL has just relaunched its Travel Kind campaign across the London transport network this summer, reminding people to use headphones.

The phenomenon has grown as we become ever more connected. Figures published in July by Ofcom show that mobile data use has increased by 13% year-on-year in the UK. 5G is being rolled out across the country, meaning that more people can get faster connectivity while travelling. And research has found that many data packages have become cheaper, meaning customers are less likely to have to ration their data use when out and about.

So as we become ever more online in public, will we see increasing attempts to clamp down on loudcasting? Or will it end up becoming as normal a part of our soundscape as the hum of passing traffic or the roar of a plane's engine thousands of feet above us?

News.title: Walk-in mental health centres to open in banks and libraries across England
News.content:
People in England needing immediate care for mental health problems will be able to access specialist walk-in hubs close to their home, the government is promising.

Ministers have set out plans to create a network of nearly 200 community mental health centres and mental health A&Es by 2029.

The aim is to give those experiencing a mental health crisis or significant distress somewhere to go to get help when they need it - with plans to open dozens of the hubs in high street locations like banks and libraries.

One in five people struggle with their mental health and thousands of people turn up at A&E when they get to crisis point because they cannot find help elsewhere.

The government believes its plans, which build on pilots that have been run over recent years, will help tackle this issue and ensure people receive expert care when they need it.

The government said there will be 100 new community mental health centres opened in a variety of locations, from libraries and banks. Some will be set up in new buildings.

They will bring together existing teams of nurses, therapists and support workers.

Many of the hubs are expected to be open seven days a week and some will have short-stay bed facilities.

Six areas have trialled the approach since 2024.

The government is also pledging to set up another 59 dedicated mental health A&Es, on top of the 23 which are already operational. Many will be attached to existing A&Es.

News.title: Families express anger over jailed funeral boss's letter
News.content:
Robert Bush's letter in full:

To everyone who has been affected by my actions.

"I have spent a great deal of time thinking about the events that [sic] wish to say something directly to you.

"I know that many of you entrusted me and my business with the care of someone you loved during one of the most difficult times in your lives.

"I recognise that what happened has caused distress, upset and uncertainty for many families. I am deeply sorry.

"There are no words that can undo what has happened or take away the pain that many of you have experienced. I understand that this has affected not only your confidence in me, but also memories surrounding the loss of those closest to you.

"I accept responsibility for my failures. Looking back, I know that I should have acted differently and much sooner. I regret that I did not do so.

"I do not expect forgiveness, nor do I write this letter in the hope of reducing the serious of what has happened.

"I simply wanted you to know that I genuinely regret the consequences of my actions, and the impact they have had on so many people.

"I appreciate that every family's experience has been different, and I respect that some people may never wish to accept my apology. That is entirely understandably.

"I hope that, in time, each of you can find some peace and remember your loved one for who they were rather than for the circumstances that have followed. I am truly sorry."

The former undertaker admitted 67 offences, including 30 counts of preventing a lawful and decent burial, and theft from 12 charities.

Prosecutors said Bush ran a "shambolic and chaotic" operation at the Hessle Road premises and his "appalling" offending had caused "extreme emotional pain, anguish and upset".

On Wednesday evening, some of his victims reacted angrily to the letter.

Beverley told the court how learning that her baby Sunny Beverley-Conlin was found in a brown paper bag on the floor of the funeral parlour "will stay with me for the rest of my life".

Sunny's remains were recovered from the Hessle Road premises one year and 10 months after he was stillborn on 13 May 2022, the court heard. She was given a set of ashes by Bush the following March.

Beverley said: "Reading the letter has left me feeling nothing but anger.

"It reads as though he is apologising for our reaction and not his actions.

"I don't have the luxury of separating my memories of Sunny from what happened because the memories I do have are tied directly to the mismanagement of the final act of love I tried to give him - his funeral.

"This will haunt me for the rest of my life."
