News.title: Reform UK pledges to jail bosses employing illegal workers
News.content:
Reform UK has pledged to imprison the bosses of companies employing illegal migrants and said it would fine larger firms 10 per cent of their global revenues.

The party said its aim was to stop delivery and gig economy companies profiting from illegal workers "without consequences".

Home affairs spokesperson Zia Yusuf said "young British people are being shut out of entry level jobs and our whole economy is being undermined".

The Home Office said it was already increasing penalties for companies hiring illegal workers. A source within the department called some of Reform's proposals "empty posturing".

Reform said that if it won the next general election, it would pass a law making chief executives and directors of large companies profiting from illegal workers personally and criminally liable.

That would be regardless of their knowledge of workers' legal status.

The party said this would be similar to the personal liability of senior managers for the financial misconduct of their firms under Financial Conduct Authority rules.

Reform would also introduce a phone line for the public to report suspected illegal working or organised criminal activity, which police and other authorities, such as trading standards teams, would be required to follow up.

Reports resulting in successful prosecutions would be rewarded with a share of any fines generated.

Yusuf said the party "would introduce the toughest penalties anywhere in the world for illegal working".

Fines are already being imposed on organisations found to be in breach of immigration laws, with one council fined Â£45,000 for employing one illegal worker in June.

A Home Office source said of Reform's announcement: "The Government is already doing much of this. The rest is just empty posturing."

A spokesperson for the department added: "We are already closing the loopholes that allow illegal migrants to work in the UK by extending right to work checks to the gig economy and delivery sector.

"Employers who break the law face severe consequences, including fines of up to Â£60,000 per illegal worker, business closures, licence revocations and prison sentences of up to five years."

They added that since Labour came to power, Immigration Enforcement action has increased "to the highest level in British history, with illegal working arrests up by 83% and raids up by 77%."

News.title: Man extradited to UK and charged over alleged hit-and-run death of Keaton Slater
News.content:
A man has been charged over the alleged hit-and-run death of schoolboy Keaton Slater in Coventry more than two years ago.

Dolars Aleksanders was extradited from Latvia, where he was detained last month, and has been charged with causing death by dangerous driving, West Midlands Police said on Wednesday night.

The 23-year-old Latvian man was taken into custody after arriving in the UK and is due to appear before Birmingham Magistrates Court on Thursday.

Keaton, 12, died after being hit by a black BMW in Coventry on 14 June 2024 while on his way home from school.

News.title: Miliband says reopening Strait of Hormuz 'essential' as he meets Rubio
News.content:
Reopening the Strait of Hormuz is essential to bringing down the cost of living in the UK, Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said as he met his US counterpart Marco Rubio.

The Labour minister is in Washington for his first official one-on-one meeting with Rubio.

The pair were expected to discuss the war in Ukraine and the humanitarian crisis in Gaza.

Miliband was invited to the US capital by Rubio after they met on the sidelines of a foreign ministers' summit in the Philippines, where the former Labour leader made his debut as foreign secretary.

The White House was reported to be concerned about Prime Minister Andy Burnham's decision to hand Miliband the Foreign Office brief, given his previous criticism of US President Donald Trump as a racist and a misogynist.

When asked by the BBC if the comments would hinder his working relationship with the Trump administration, Miliband said they would not and had not been mentioned during a 90-minute meeting.

Miliband said the "productive" discussion had focused on Iran, support for Ukraine, and "how we can work towards relieving the terrible suffering we are seeing in Gaza and have a two-state solution for the security of the Israeli and Palestinian people".

Trump is also a trenchant opponent of wind farms and supports the opening up North Sea oil and use of fossil fuels, whereas in his former role as UK energy secretary, Miliband championed net zero and renewables.

Burnham has signalled a shift in North Sea oil policy, earning praise from the Oval Office, but the dynamic between Miliband and Rubio was set to be closely watched.

Last month, Washington's top diplomat in London, Warren Stephens, said Miliband had been "wrong" in 2016 to call Trump "a racist, misogynistic self-confessed groper" and added "hopefully his views have changed".

Following their meeting, US state department spokesman Tommy Pigott said: "The two discussed the importance of Europe taking on a greater role in its own security.

"They reiterated their shared commitment to safe transit in the Strait of Hormuz and ensuring Iran never develops or obtains a nuclear weapon."

In a statement after the meeting, Miliband thanked Rubio for a "warm, productive meeting" and said he was "hopeful" that the Strait may be re-opened.

"The number one priority for this government is to tackle the cost of living crisis that people are facing and my job as foreign secretary most immediately is to work with our closest ally the United States on getting a lasting ceasefire in relation to the Iran war.

"We are working night and day to make that happen - that was a large part of our discussions today - I am hopeful that this may happen, but we are not there yet."

He added: "People should be in no doubt, I know as foreign secretary that the British people are worried about what's happened to petrol prices, diesel prices, energy bills, and the single biggest thing we can do is get that ceasefire in relation to Iran."

The strategic sea route, which had been open before the US and Israel launched the war in February, has been a flashpoint in the Middle East conflict and disruption to trade has driven up fuel and food prices.

Miliband added: "We also discussed standing together with Ukraine in the face of Putin's war, and spoke about the intolerable situation in Gaza and the urgent need to address the humanitarian situation there, as we work towards a lasting peace for Palestinians and Israelis."

News.title: Ex neo-Nazi activist withdraws as Tory election candidate
News.content:
A former neo-Nazi selected by the Conservatives to fight a council election next year has pulled out after a backlash against his candidacy.

Joshua Bonehill-Paine was convicted of racially harassing Jewish former Labour MP Luciana Berger in 2016, while already serving a separate jail sentence for sharing antisemitic posts.

Tory leader Kemi Badenoch had defended the decision to select him as a candidate for the new Somerset Council seat of Crewkerne South, saying he had been rehabilitated and her party "believes in second chances".

But Bonehill-Paine said he had now withdrawn his candidacy, and had been offered a position as an anti-extremism adviser to the party.

In a social media post, he said the position with the Conservative Party's Culture and Integration Commission would focus on advising on how to prevent young men from being radicalised.

Berger, who now sits as Baroness Berger in the House of Lords, described the appointment as an "insult," adding that making him a party adviser was "no better than allowing him to stand as a council candidate".

The position as an anti-extremism adviser to the party is unpaid, the BBC understands.

Bonehill-Paine spent three years in prison after he was jailed in 2015 for posting antisemitic material ahead of a planned neo-Nazi rally. He was convicted of racially harassing then-Labour MP Berger the following year.

News.title: Family 'devastated' by death of girl, 9, as man charged with murder
News.content:
The family of a nine-year-old girl who died after being found seriously injured in Arbroath have said they are "devastated" at her loss, as a man appeared in court charged with her murder.

Minnie Merriman, from West Yorkshire, died in Dundee's Ninewells Hospital on Monday.

A 35-year-old man, who police said was known to the girl, has appeared in court charged with her murder.

Christopher Rice from Wakefield, West Yorkshire, made no plea during an appearance in private at Forfar Sheriff Court and was remanded in custody.

News.title: Woman arrested after four stabbed in central London
News.content:
A 47-year-old woman has been arrested after four men were stabbed in Covent Garden in central London, the Metropolitan Police said.

The men, aged 34, 39, 42 and 52, were taken to hospital after emergency services were called to reports of a stabbing in Endell Street at about 12:30 BST.

The force said two men remain in hospital with injuries not thought to be life threatening or life changing while the other two have been discharged.

The woman was arrested on suspicion of possession of an offensive weapon and assault. The Met said it was believed to have been a mental health-related incident.

Ch Supt Jason Stewart said: "Officers responded within minutes of this incident after receiving a number of reports.

"While still at an early stage of the investigation, we would like to reassure the community that we currently believe this to be an isolated, mental-health related incident."

He added a "visible police presence" would remain in the area while evidence was gathered.

News.title: Student loan repayment rates an 'unsustainable burden', chancellor told
News.content:
More than 120 MPs and peers have asked the chancellor to carry out an "urgent review" of the student loan repayment system.

An open letter coordinated by the campaign group Rethink Repayment says the current set-up places an "unsustainable burden on the next generation of workers".

Among the cross-party signatories are MPs with their own Plan 2 student loans, which have come under particular scrutiny this year.

Last week, Education Secretary Lucy Powell said the interest rate on those loans was "egregious" and the issue was at the top of her in-tray.

Current and former students have different student loan plans depending on where they live in the UK and when they went to university.

The letter to Chancellor John Healey does not specify a particular plan signatories would like to be reformed, nor does it name a particular nation.

However, the debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were taken out by students in England between September 2012 and July 2023 and are still issued in Wales. Graduates pay back what they earn above the repayment threshold at a rate of 9%.

The letter says that "successive governments' adjustments to repayment thresholds â together with high interest and marginal tax rates â are placing an unsustainable burden on the next generation of workers".

It says many middle-income graduates "see less than half of any hard-earned pay rise due to a combination of income tax, national insurance and student loan repayments".

It adds: "We are united in the belief that the current repayment framework requires urgent review... to ensure it is fair, sustainable, and supportive of aspiration."

News.title: Gary Glitter appears in court over historical sex offence charges
News.content:
Dressed in a blue shirt and wearing sunglasses, Glitter appeared by video link from His Majesty's Prison Channings Wood for the 11-minute hearing.

Under his real name, Gadd was told of the charges against him and spoke only to confirm his name and date of birth.

The prosecutor, Jonathan Polnay KC, told the court that Gadd said in a police interview he did not know the complainant, and that the allegations against him were false.

He also told the court that the offences involved one person, and are said to have taken place between the years of 1978 and 1981 when the complainant was eight to 11 years old.

He said she lived near where Glitter lived and that was how he came to know her. She says he gave her chocolate and that he invited her into his house where the offences occurred.

The allegations were first reported to the Metropolitan Police on 9 January 2025 and an investigation into the circumstances was launched.

Gadd was first interviewed on 22 July last year in relation to the investigation.

The 82-year-old was one of the biggest pop stars of the 1970s with a string of number one hits.

The Met said in July that the alleged victim was being supported by specialist officers and had been made aware that Glitter had been charged.

The singer is currently being held in HMP Channings Wood in Devon.

A week after calling Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey “abysmal”, classicist Emily Wilson has doubled down on her criticism, describing it as “visually stunning” but “emotionally empty”.

Writing in The Atlantic, a week after her blistering review of the film for the London Review of Books, Wilson said Nolan’s adaptation ultimately fails to live up to its own ethical ambitions.

“Nolan’s Odyssey is itself a kind of Trojan horse,” Wilson wrote. “The script grandly insists on the importance of human kindness, while the camera shows us an entirely different set of values.”

“In these times of hatred and misinformation, we need more than the ‘apparent magic’ of deceptive images. We need art that is truthful about the costs and the necessity of compassion,” she wrote.

She added those lessons were present in Homer and Virgil but “elided by Nolan’s visually stunning, emotionally empty film”.

Released last month, The Odyssey is Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek epic, following Odysseus’ perilous journey home to Ithaca after the Trojan War. Matt Damon stars as the king of Ithaca, with Anne Hathaway as his wife Penelope and Tom Holland as their son Telemachus. The ensemble cast also includes Zendaya as the goddess Athena, Charlize Theron as the nymph Calypso, Robert Pattinson as the suitor Antinous and Himesh Patel as Odysseus’ second-in-command, Eurylochus.

The film has received rave reviews and is expected to be a major Oscar contender, with The Independent’s Clarisse Loughrey calling The Odyssey Nolan’s “best film to date” in her five-star review.

open image in gallery Classicist Emily Wilson has doubled down on her of criticism of Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , describing it as ‘visually stunning’ but ‘emotionally empty’ ( Universal Pictures )

In The Odyssey, the Trojan Horse is presented as the ultimate breach of what characters repeatedly call “Zeus’ law”, a principle of hospitality and kindness towards strangers.

Wilson argued that the idea never fully makes sense because the film “does not explain what ‘hospitality’ has to do with a narrative situation in which the Greeks have been besieging Troy for 10 years already”.

“The Trojans are not their hosts but their enemies in war,” she wrote.

Wilson wrote that the film is more interested in how war is staged than in what it does to people.

She contrasts Nolan’s adaptation with Homer’s Odyssey and Virgil’s Aeneid, arguing that both poems are deeply interested in how people deceive, why others believe them and the human consequences that follow. Nolan’s film, by contrast, is “not interested in the social or psychological questions of how people deceive and are deceived”.

Instead, she wrote that the film dwells on “the logistics” of hauling the horse ashore, moving weapons and breaching city gates. “The script tells us loudly that people matter,” she wrote, “but the camera shows us that what matters is the mechanical challenge of moving objects through space.”

Wilson also revisited one of the strongest criticisms from her original review, questioning Nolan’s decision to film scenes in Dakhla, in the Moroccan-occupied territory of Western Sahara, without the consent of the Indigenous Sahrawi people. The production drew criticism last year from Sahrawi activists and the Western Sahara International Film Festival (FiSahara), who argued that filming in the disputed territory risked legitimising Morocco’s decades-long occupation.

She argued that the choice sits uneasily with a film concerned with the ethics of invading other people’s homes, calling it “the lack of seriousness in Nolan’s thinking about his themes”.

open image in gallery Released last month, The Odyssey is Nolan’s adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek epic, following Odysseus’ perilous journey home to Ithaca after the Trojan War ( Universal Pictures )

In her previous review, Wilson had written that Nolan’s film strips away much of what has made Homer’s epic endure for nearly 3,000 years, and “lacks psychological, emotional, political and ethical depth”.

Wilson, who became the first woman to publish a complete English translation of The Odyssey in 2017, had previously been named by Nolan as an influence on the film. In an interview with Empire magazine in November 2025, the director said it was the opening line of Wilson's translation – “Tell me about a complicated man” – that unlocked his approach to Odysseus.

Her review even led to novelist Joyce Carol Oates coming to Nolan’s defence, who criticised Wilson’s “tone of dismissal & haughty superiority” and accused her of speaking in “the crude language of MAGA folks” instead of engaging with his interpretation of Homer “in a collegial manner”.

The Odyssey is screening in theatres now.

Sudan’s ongoing war is threatening the integrity of its ancient Meroe pyramids, a UNESCO World Heritage Site known for its unique and angular architecture, as preservation efforts have completely halted.

“The site may face a disaster and collapses are possible,” warned archaeologist Mahmoud Suleiman.

Meroe, located some 200 kilometers (125 miles) north of the capital Khartoum, comprises over 200 pyramids built between 800 B.C. and 350 A.D. as royal tombs for the rulers of the Kingdom of Kush.

“The sand has thickened heavily on the pyramids and even inside the temples, and the grass grows thick,” Mustafa Ahmed, one of the guards at Meroe, told The Associated Press as he made his way through sand dunes on site. “The pyramids have deteriorated greatly and stones have begun to fall.”

Mohamed Mubarak, an antiquities inspector, said salt, released from accumulated sand, has collected inside the funerary temples and is degrading the "inherently fragile” stones, risking the erosion of ancient inscriptions.

“Climate change, war leading to the dispersal of the workforce, and the difficulty for foreign missions to continue their work amid the country’s security instability ... all contributed to the significant deterioration of the site,” said Suleiman, the archaeologist.

Sudan’s deadly conflict, which erupted in April 2023, has destroyed multiple of the country’s historical sites and museums. UNESCO warned in April that cultural and historical sites are under growing threat, with over 100 cultural sites damaged, and at least 22 museums looted or destroyed since the onset of the war.

Jeremy Clarkson has claimed that he’ll work between 15 and 20 hours a day on Diddly Squat in the summer – and yet, he doesn’t “actually get paid” for what he harvests.

The Clarkson’s Farm star, who originally bought his Cotswolds farm in 2008, began running it himself in 2019 and has since been vocal about the difficulties of making a profit as a farmer. Last month, he revealed that it’s become “impossible” to make money from growing food on the farm.

In his latest newspaper column, Clarkson shed more light on farm life, revealing that he’ll “work non-stop” on Diddly Squat in the summer and yet it’s still “cheaper to go on an expensive holiday”.

Writing in The Sun, he said that farmers are not able to book a summer holiday as it’s “impossible” to know when the harvest will be. “This means the farmer is forced to stay at home for the summer, looking at Instagram pictures of all his non-farming friends as they frolic on boats and in bars in the sun-drenched Mediterranean.

open image in gallery Clarkson shared the ‘unpleasant’ reality of working on a farm ( Prime Video )

“Sounds terrible, yes? Well it isn’t. Some jobs on the farm are unpleasant. Sexing rabbits is annoyingly difficult, and disposing of dead piglets is heartbreaking. But I’ve been harvesting all week, and this job is an absolute joy.”

He added that he wakes up at 4am to “work non-stop for 15 to 20 hours at a stretch” and while it’s “hot and dirty out there”, he can’t get enough of it.

“Finally, you turn off the engines and in the golden-hour silence that results, you crack open an ice cold bottle of beer and gulp at it as the sun goes down. I’ve drunk beers in many exotic and beautiful locations over the years, but none of them match the beer you treat yourself to after a hard day’s harvesting,” he said.

“The only slight fly in the ointment is that thanks to the hot summer and this Government’s strange hatred of farmers, you don’t actually get paid for the wheat and the barley you’ve harvested. In fact, I worked out this morning that it’d be cheaper to go on an expensive holiday.”

The Independent has contacted the Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs for comment.

open image in gallery Jeremy Clarkson with his partner Lisa Hogan, pictured in 2024 ( Getty )

Last month, Clarkson called for action from the government on farming matters, revealing that he’s left 200 acres of his farm bare as it would be “impossible” to make money from it. “We knew that if we planted it with wheat or barley, we would definitely make a loss,” he said.

Since taking up farming, Clarkson has become actively engaged with agricultural policy; in May 2024, he challenged government planning reforms, advocating for farmers to convert agricultural buildings into homes and shops.

Meanwhile, in the last series of Clarkson’s Farm, viewers watched as the presenter protested against the government’s proposals to increase inheritance tax by 20 per cent on agricultural assets worth more than £1m. After the protests, the government increased the threshold from £1m to £2.5m.

The recent series also saw Clarkson reveal that he had been diagnosed with cancer. He shared on the show that his cancer was aggressive but had been caught at a “really early” stage, and later said that a post-treatment test two months ago found no indication of cancer.

Morale is plummeting on an American aircraft carrier that's running short of food and other supplies as its exhausted crew wages President Donald Trump's war against Iran, worried family members say.

Sailors and Marines serving on the USS Abraham Lincoln have told relatives about being served a half-cup of rice and two tortillas for a meal, and said the ship's store often lacks soap, deodorant and toothpaste, MS NOW reported Wednesday.

Crew members are also worn out by working long, grueling shifts, with some rarely getting a day off, and described broken toilets, moldy showers without hot water and no laundry service for weeks at a time, relatives said.

“The morale is not good,” said Bonnie York, whose stepson is aboard the Lincoln. “Apparently, the ship’s doctor or therapist said they need to hit port soon or people are going to start, you know, losing their minds.”

The Lincoln and its more than 5,000 personnel arrived in the Middle East in January, after leaving its home port of San Diego in November, according to MS NOW.

open image in gallery ‘The morale is not good’ on the USS Abraham Lincoln, says Bonnie York, whose stepson is serving on the aircraft carrier in the Middle East (pictured) ( US Navy )

Trump launched the war against Iran without congressional approval on February 28 and initially said it would last four to five weeks. On Wednesday, he said a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and help end the war could be announced this week, according to The Associated Press.

Navy veteran Brett Snow, whose son is also on the Lincoln, warned that conditions on the ship could lead to disaster, noting that an aircraft carrier was an extremely hazardous workplace even during peacetime.

“It’s the most dangerous place in the world already, and now you’re grinding it out, day in and day out, with no breaks,” Snow said. “It’s an environment that’s ripe for accidents.”

An unidentified father, who's also a Navy veteran, reportedly said his son described seeing holes that have worn through the ship's deck.

Representative Sara Jacobs, a California Democrat who represents the Lincoln’s home port of San Diego, told MS NOW she was “deeply worried” about the crew's “exhaustion and mental health, because history has shown it can lead to serious consequences, including increased risk of suicide.”

open image in gallery The flight deck of Nimitz-class aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln. Navy veteran Brett Snow, whose son is serving on the Lincoln, says an aircraft carrier is ‘an environment that’s ripe for accidents’ ( Getty )

The Navy didn't immediately respond to an inquiry from The Independent. Commander Joseph Hontz told MS NOW there were no holes in the deck and said the crew has repaired wear and tear when needed.

Hontz, spokesperson for the Navy's Fifth Fleet, also acknowledged the strain on the ship's more than 5,000 crew members but said the Lincoln “remains fully capable of meeting all mission tasking.”

“Though more than 250 days on deployment is challenging for the crew and their equipment, they remain resilient and ready to accomplish any tasking given to them,” he said.

In April, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth denied there were food shortages on the Lincoln and the USS Tripoli, calling it “fake news” after USA Today published photos of small portions of what it called “gross” food served to sailors and Marines.

Nicole Conrad, whose son is serving on the Lincoln, told MS NOW she wanted Hegseth to personally check on the conditions there.

“Go visit. If you want to sit here and you want to say that Trump is taking care of the soldiers, go yourself,” she said.

Conrad and the two other parents who spoke to MS NOW said they had voted for Trump but were unhappy with his decision to go to war against Iran.

open image in gallery The parents of the sailors say they voted for President Donald Trump but are unhappy with his decision to go to war against Iran ( AP )

“He put our nose in a war that we shouldn’t be in,” Conrad said.

York said she voted for Trump “because he said he wasn't going to war” but now believed “we are sacrificing for something that none of us want to be a part of, essentially.”

“I don’t think we’re safer,” she said. “I think we’ve depleted a lot of things. I think we’ve pushed our military to the edge.”

Snow, the Navy veteran, said he agreed with Trump that Iran should be denied nuclear weapons, but added that he didn't think the president's strategy was working.

“I don’t know if we’re ever going to be able to achieve any kind of reasonable — anything that even comes close to what Americans might consider a victory,” he said.

Over two dozen new human ancestor fossils unearthed at a Spanish cave site suggest these first Europeans may have engaged in cannibalism 850,000 years ago.

More than 30 years after the discovery of the first fossils attributed to the prehistoric human species Homo antecessor, new finds at the cave site of Gran Dolina continue to reshape our understanding of the species.

Ongoing excavations have found that the adult remains of Homo antecessor buried here preserve cut marks produced during the processing of the bodies, indicating they were victims of cannibalism.

The findings shed more light on the biology, development, social relationships, and behaviour of Homo antecessor around 850,000 years ago.

open image in gallery New fossil reveals a much more complete Homo antecessor population and confirms that cannibalism also affected adults ( IPHES )

At the cave site, researchers unearthed several fossil bones of the human ancestor species, including a fragment of the temporal bone, several vertebrae, hand and foot phalanges, three teeth and long bones such as the first inner forearm bone ever recovered from the site, as well as fragments of leg bones, tibia, femur and humerus.

“Each excavation season helps us complete a puzzle that still has many missing pieces. The increase in the number of individuals, and especially the addition of more adults, allows us to begin understanding this population from a much more complete perspective than ever before,” excavation co-director Andreu Ollé said.

“For the first time, we can approach its demographic structure with a level of representativeness that we simply did not have until now,” Dr Ollé said.

Compared to previous fossil recoveries, there has been a substantial increase in the number of adult individuals documented at the site, researchers say.

This has helped better reconstruct the species population in a way that is far more balanced and demographically representative, they say.

open image in gallery New Homo antecessor fossil unearthed at Spanish cave site ( IPHES )

Many of the unearthed remains, including those of juvenile and adult individuals, had cut marks produced during the processing of the bodies, hinting at cannibalistic practices among the population.

“The discovery of more adult individuals, some of whom also bear cut marks, demonstrates that cannibalism was not restricted to younger individuals,” said Palmira Saladié, a researcher at the Catalan Institute for Human Palaeoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES).

“More importantly, however, it provides us with a much more representative population for understanding the biology, demography and behaviour of Homo antecessor,” Dr Saladié said.

At the cave site, researchers also unearthed stone tools made from flint, quartzite, sandstone and quartz, as well as remains belonging to hyenas, beavers, deer, bovids, horses and rhinoceroses.

open image in gallery Stone tool found at the site ( IPHES )

Taken together, the stone tools, animal remains, and human fossils make the cave site one of the finest archaeological records in Europe for understanding the continent’s earliest human populations.

“The significance of Gran Dolina extends far beyond its human fossils. The relationship between the stone tools, faunal remains and the bones of Homo antecessor allows us to reconstruct a human occupation site from 850,000 years ago with extraordinary detail,” Dr Ollé said.

“We have only just begun excavating this new area, and the first results already demonstrate its enormous scientific potential,” said IPHES director Marina Mosquera.

The Israeli military said Thursday that two of its soldiers were killed in combat in southern Lebanon in the first Israeli deaths since the implementation of a shaky truce between Israel and the Iran-backed Lebanese militant group Hezbollah in June.

Four other soldiers were wounded, the military said. The deaths had been reported by Israeli media a day earlier.

The Israeli army launched strikes Wednesday in southern Lebanon in response to what it described as Hezbollah’s violation of the ceasefire and issued a call for residents of the village of Mansouri to flee — the first such warning Israel has issued in Lebanon for weeks.

There was no immediate statement from Hezbollah.

The escalation came as Lebanese and Israeli negotiators met in Rome to discuss implementation of a June 26 deal under which Israeli forces are supposed to withdraw from areas they occupy in southern Lebanon and allow the Lebanese army to take control, in exchange for Hezbollah’s disarmament.

The latest Israel-Hezbollah war erupted on March 2, when Hezbollah fired rockets across the border two days after the U.S. and Israel launched their attacks on Iran.

A shaky truce between Israel and Hezbollah has largely held since June 20, but Israeli forces have continued to occupy swaths of southern Lebanon and to carry out periodic airstrikes and shelling.

News.title: Iran president admits interaction with supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei is ‘very difficult’
News.content:
Your support helps us to tell the story Read more Support Now From reproductive rights to climate change to Big Tech, The Independent is on the ground when the story is developing. Whether it's investigating the financials of Elon Musk's pro-Trump PAC or producing our latest documentary, 'The A Word', which shines a light on the American women fighting for reproductive rights, we know how important it is to parse out the facts from the messaging. At such a critical moment in US history, we need reporters on the ground. Your donation allows us to keep sending journalists to speak to both sides of the story. The Independent is trusted by Americans across the entire political spectrum. And unlike many other quality news outlets, we choose not to lock Americans out of our reporting and analysis with paywalls. We believe quality journalism should be available to everyone, paid for by those who can afford it. Your support makes all the difference. Read more

Interaction with Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, is currently “very difficult”, Iran’s president has said.

Khamenei, 56, has not been seen in public since assuming the role after his father, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was killed in February in a joint US-Israeli air strike.

His absence from visibility has prompted widespread speculation about the state of his health.

President Masoud Pezeshkian made the cryptic comment in an interview on state television but gave no further detail and it was not clear what he meant by “interaction”.

Top Iranian officials told the New York Times earlier this year that the new supreme leader had been gravely wounded but that he was mentally in good health.

A picture on a wall of Iran's Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei who has not been seen in public since he became supreme leader ( AFP/Getty )

According to the report, his face and lips were badly burnt, making speech difficult, but one of his hands was operated on and he was gradually regaining function.

Khamenei reportedly required plastic surgery to his face and was awaiting a new prosthetic leg.

In conflicting reports in May, Iran said Khamenei was suffering from a “small scratch” behind his ear after initial reports that he suffered life-altering injuries in US-Israeli attacks.

But the regime said he was otherwise in “full health” despite injuries to his kneecap and back.

The president said earlier that ​Tehran ⁠would ⁠support any ​initiative ⁠or decision by Palestinian ‌leaders in ⁠indirect talks between militant group Hamas and Israel, ‌according to state ​media.

A report by an Iranian media site on Monday said that Khamenei had warned Pezeshkian that he (Khamenei) would accept the Iranian president's resignation if he resubmitted it.

In May, Pezeshkian was reported to have argued that he could no longer fulfil his constitutional responsibilities and had asked to step down immediately.

The Islamic regime has not released any videos or audio of the supreme leader.

One Iranian media report claimed it was feared this could reveal Khamenei's whereabouts and condition.

Khamenei, considered a hardline conservative cleric with links to Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, is instructed by some of Iran’s most powerful scholars in Qom, where he trained to be a cleric.

During the Iran-Iraq war, he served in the Iranian military between 1987 and 1988.

News.title: ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality
News.content:
Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

No Saliba a concern

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

News.title: Ebola outbreak outpacing containment effort, WHO chief warns
News.content:
Caused by the rare Bundibugyo strain of Ebola, for which there are no vaccines or treatments, it has been extremely difficult to contain, according to experts on the ground.

“The outbreak is spreading faster than our scale-up of the response, with new cases doubling in some hotspots over the past week alone,” Dr Tedros said on X.

Part of the difficulty is that the virus was circulating undetected for weeks before the outbreak was formally declared in mid-May, leaving health officials even now racing to catch up with the spread.

Prof Placide Mbala, director of research, clinical trials and innovation at Africa CDC, told the Telegraph: “It’s mostly the fact we arrived a bit late. It took us some time before we detected this virus outbreak. And when we detected the outbreak, we already had a total of I can say more than 200 suspected cases. It’s been difficult to catch up. That’s where we are.”

While the DRC has a wealth of experience in tackling haemorrhagic fever outbreaks, the effects of that initial delay are still being felt.

Prof Mbala said: “We have some experience dealing with the cases, the labs, the communication, the infection prevention and control.

“We have some experience... But my observation is that we were very slow, and it’s why we’re in this situation.

“We are slow detecting the people, slow responding, we are slow deploying people, we are slow to recruit the community healthcare workers to improve contact tracing, we are slow to deploy the safe burials.”

DRC’s largest outbreak had previously been from 2018 to 2020, when 3,481 cases were recorded.

The West Africa outbreak recorded 28,616 cases and 11,310 deaths according to the WHO.

Prof Mbala said insecurity was also severely hampering attempts to curb the virus. The outbreak epicentre is in Ituri province, which has been wracked by ethnic strife for decades and is also home to militias competing to control mining.

He said: “There are many, many mining groups controlling most of the mining places. We have a big issue with those places, because they are places where the response team cannot go.”

Medics and aid workers have also been undermined by violent public distrust of their efforts.

Locals in the area have either doubted the existence of the virus, or have accused health teams of deliberately spreading the infection, or somehow benefiting from it.

More than a dozen health facilities have been set alight and several health workers have been killed.

Prof Mbala said: “The local people, they also sometimes are very upset, because they believe that it’s a kind of a business, and people who are coming here, they are getting a lot of money, [so] don’t want this disease to stop.”

He said he hoped that immunity was starting to rise in some areas and this would start to curb transmission.

However there was also a risk that people fleeing the outbreak would spread the virus further afield.

He said: “The second scenario is the fact we are seeing people moving from the affected area to new areas, to run away from the response team because they do not want to go to the treatment centre.

“And in complicity with their family members living in other areas, they are now the ones who are spreading the disease to new areas

“So we’ll see new places affected because people are moving around from the affected zone to the non-affected zone.”

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat
News.content:
Chelsea 0 Juventus 1

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

News.title: The underground lab where ‘princess mosquitoes’ are treated like royalty
News.content:
Beneath the grand Art Deco headquarters of the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine lies a vast labyrinth inhabited by weird and wonderful creatures.

In this maze of subterranean labs, store rooms and corridors live colonies of disease-bearing insects and arachnids from all over the world, from bed bugs, sand flies and microscopic dust mites to the so-called kissing bugs that spread Chagas disease – a sinister condition that can cause its victims to drop dead of heart failure without warning, albeit decades after the first (silent) infection.

Behind a series of doors, contained in stacks of mesh boxes, you can even find the flies that spread trachoma, the Dickensian eye disease that is still a leading cause of blindness around the world. But be warned: entering the room is not for the faint of heart – the flies feed on human excrement and the smell is impossible to forget.

There are also many varieties of mosquito, including several species of the Anopheles genus that spread malaria, Culex and Aedes mosquitoes that are also vectors for human and animal diseases, and even Toxorhynchites, perhaps better known as the elephant mosquito, a friendly giant which doesn’t bite people but preys on other mosquitoes.

These animals have been studied intensely since the insectaries were established in the building’s vaults in the 1960s, underpinning many breakthroughs in the control, surveillance, and understanding of vector-borne diseases in the developing world.

LSHTM researchers are now looking closer to home. They have established the UK’s first laboratory colony of Aedes vexans mosquitoes, a species native to the British isles, to study whether they could harbour diseases like West Nile virus, Rift Valley fever, Zika or Japanese encephalitis.

News.title: What I saw in a week on the front line of Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
News.content:
May 15 and 16, 2026

It is the weekend, a small moment to rest, although there is still a lot of work waiting for me. A week in the field does not mean that work in Kabul stops. I try to catch up on my emails and have a planned online interview for an international staff position – since in Europe, Friday is a normal working day. I also review parts of new proposals for donors and our financial planning.

On Saturday, however, I take a short break. Together with the base management team in Helmand, we visit a historical site called Qala-e-Bost, believed to have been built around 3,000 years ago. It is a rare moment to step away from work, followed by lunch with the team.

May 17, 2026

Sunday morning, the first working day of the week, we visit Basrhan Sub Health Centre, run by one of our local partners. As a nurse and former nurse trainer, I feel very much in my element in these health centres. It allows me to engage easily with the team and discuss their work.

I speak with the outreach officer and the vaccinator. They explain that this facility supports 18 outreach locations, each visited at least once a month. They provide vaccinations, raise awareness, and connect communities to the health centre. These visits often take place in simple settings, like mosques.

Immunisation is now well accepted. In the beginning, there was some resistance, but trust has grown over time. Every child is tracked, and if a child misses a vaccination, community health volunteers follow up at home. For extra polio vaccinations, this is carefully recorded by marking a finger of the child – helping ensure that no child is missed. The goal is clear: a polio-free Afghanistan.

I also speak with a mother. She is wearing a burka, so I cannot see her face. She tells me she is 22 years old and holds her 12-month-old son on her lap. She came because he has a fever, but I see a healthy child – something that stands out after my time in the TFU.

She brings her child regularly for follow-up and growth monitoring and the child has never been in a treatment program for malnutrition. She speaks positively about the services. “We are lucky,” she says. “The staff treat us well, and we have access to care in our community.”

News.title: World’s first seahorse hospital fights to protect them from extinction
News.content:
With careful precision, marine biologist Linda Albonetti extracts a 10cm-long injured seahorse – a heavily pregnant male – from an aquarium tank to apply healing ointment to its wound.

Linda, 29, coordinator at the world’s first specialist seahorse hospital, is currently caring for around 50 of these tiny creatures, all of which were brought in by local fishing crews after becoming snagged in their nets.

The seahorse will be kept for a few more days before it is released back into the Adriatic Sea, giving it time to recover from the cut to the soft, bony plates that form its outer carapace.

What the team here are doing is a literal drop in the ocean, a small attempt to fight back against the potential extinction of these remarkable fish.

In Europe and around countries like Indonesia, they are being poached in their millions for sale to a voracious Asian traditional medicine market where they are consumed as an aphrodisiac and alleged cure for impotence, asthma and kidney problems.

“There is definitely a downward trend in the overall seahorse population because they are being collected for the Asian market,” says Linda. “Technically, they cannot be exported to countries such as China, but there is no specific law preventing that trade. They do not have the same protections as sea turtles, for example.

“It is not happening in this part of Italy yet, but it is further south, off the Mediterranean coast. That is why it is so important that we monitor their numbers and maintain a good relationship with the local fishermen.”

News.title: The 13 best castle hotels in England
News.content:
Few places capture the imagination quite like a castle, and England is home to some of the most remarkable places to spend the night. If it’s not the romance of waking up in a canopied four-poster bed, or losing ourselves in centuries-old tapestries and visceral oil paintings, we are lured by tales of brave knights and plotting dignitaries, duplicitous royals and ghosts parleying secrets in the hallways.

Part of the magic is spending an afternoon wandering grounds and gardens followed by evenings in front of a roaring fire, or dining in a banquet hall that may have hosted medieval kings and queens. While not every castle has crenellated battlements, glistening moats or royal connections, each stony stronghold on our list has something special that makes it worth travelling for. In this modern age that might include a spa, fine-dining restaurant or extra touches like free admission to exhibitions and museum tours. Here’s our pick of the best castle hotels in England.

News.title: Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds
News.content:
Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Bombshell documents expose Fifa boss Infantino’s undercover partnership to launch rival Super League and sideline clubs
Sports.content:
BOMBSHELL documents exposed Gianni Infantino plotted to partner with the breakaway European Super League.

And it was even proposed to name it the ‘Fifa Super League’.



News broke in April 2021 of the 20-team league proposed to shake up club football.

Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham all signed up to the closed-shop division.



It would have created a new rival competition featuring 15 permanent members – also including co-founders Real Madrid, Barcelona, Atletico, Inter Milan, AC Milan and Juventus – and five qualifying teams.

But intense, furious backlash to the plans from excluded teams, football governing bodies and fans across the world saw the Super League collapse and scrapped.

At the time, Fifa president Infantino told Uefa’s congress that his organisation condemned the proposed new league.

He said: “At Fifa, we can only strongly disapprove the creation of a Super League which is a closed shop, which is a breakaway from the current institutions, from the leagues, from the associations, from Uefa and from Fifa, which is outside of the system.

“There is no doubt whatsoever of Fifa’s disapproval for this.”

However, according to The Guardian, shocking files now allege he was very much part of the breakaway rebellion.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

The report claims a term sheet – usually a precurser to a ratified and definitive contract – dated in October 2020 suggests naming the new league with Fifa’s branding.

The Guardian also suggests Fifa were willing to sideline its member associations in pushing plans to alter international windows and bypassed federations over Club World Cup proposals.

The Club World Cup would have been staged annually and directly connected to the new Super League.

And the damning documents, according to The Guardian, suggest Fifa are referred to as ‘WO1’ – a term used for high-ranking officers in the British army.



The report explains the term sheet said the Super League “is open to discuss naming the competition WO1 SL”.

It also stated Fifa would be “granted a preferred equity stake in the Super League”, thus ensuring the power to make decisions on format and calendar changes plus the appointment of a chief executive and distribution of funds.

When approached by SunSport for comment, Fifa sent links to articles posted in 2021 including Infantino’s comments to the Uefa congress and a signed statement from the Fifa boss plus the presidents of the six continental confederations refusing to recognise any unafiliated, rival competitions.

The outlandish expose comes a week after Infantino’s plans to auction off stakes in the World Cup were made public.

The angry reaction from confederations, national FAs and even many within Fifa prompted a swift and embarrassing U-turn for the Swiss chief, who is now desperately clinging on to power after a humiliating week.



He is holed up in Rabat, Morocco, where he staged an emergency crisis meeting with Fifa big-wigs.

Infantino apologised but vowed to fight on as the head of world football.

Further reports – denied by Fifa – suggest Infantino has offered Morocco the World Cup final in 2030 in return for public backing, as he still awaits support from 2034 hosts Saudi Arabia.

Meanwhile, Portugal legend Luis Figo tweeted on Wednesday: “Today I join others from across our game and call for Gianni Infantino to resign as Fifa President.

“Infantino has debased the office that he promised to elevate.



“He has lied, deceived and tried to feather his own nest at the expense of the game he is supposed to serve.

“He has lost the support of his senior staff, his closest advisers, the vast majority of people who devote their lives to this sport and even, it would seem, the Fifa Peace Prize winner.

“It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football. He should go. Now. #Infantinout”

That came 24 hours after the Jordan FA boss Prince Ali Bin Al Hussein accused Infantino and Fifa of “blackmail”.

Prince Ali wrote: “There is no shortage of issues regarding Fifa.



“We have been waiting for reward money for our players since December for the Arab Cup in Qatar, which is a Fifa event.

“The money our team should receive for having reached the final has not been delivered yet, while at the same time Fifa brags about how many billions they have in reserve.

“It is clear the problem really is with leadership.

“For months, Fifa has been refusing to help us on any of these or other matters – until it was verbally communicated to me during the World Cup that if I endorsed Infantino it would go a long way to helping our FA out.

“We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values.



“We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that.”

Sports.title: Mo Salah left in awe as 25,000 Trabzonspor fans party wildly with flares to welcome Liverpool legend after free transfer
Sports.content:
MO SALAH was given a hero’s welcome by 25,000 fans after agreeing a mega-money move to Turkey’s Trabzonspor.

The Liverpool legend jetted in from his holiday on Greek island Mykonos to sign a two-year deal worth £363,000 a week — AFTER TAX.



And the Egyptian King, 34, was blown away by his reception at Trabzon Airport.

Salah was treated to hundreds of flares and fireworks as he proudly wore his new No10 shirt, the number he wears for his beloved Egypt, after ditching his iconic No11 from his Liverpool days.



As the party raged on, Salah said: “It is incredible to have these fans here now.

“The reception was unbelievable, so I am very happy to be here.



“I can’t put it into words, but the fans here show so much love…25,000 people. I don’t know if I have seen that before at an airport!

“But it is a great feeling and shows a lot of love. So I am really happy about this, for sure. I am looking forward to joining the team.

“Everywhere I go I always try to win something. Hopefully, we can do something good in the league and Europe as well.”

Salah has been on the hunt for a new club since appearing for Egypt at this summer’s World Cup.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Talks with Trabzonspor accelerated this week and led to the winger flying in from Greek island Mykonos.

Salah, who will wear the No10 shirt, travelled to Istanbul via a private jet and he was greeted by a small number of supporters and media.

The Egyptian then went to Acibadem Maslak Hospital to undergo a medical, before flying to Trabzon.

It was at the airport there where the 34-year-old was mobbed by fans, who set off flares and fireworks.



Trabzonspor had earlier called for calm via a statement on social media, but the surrounding roads were gridlocked by the time Salah arrived at around 9pm local time.

The signing is a major coup for the Turkish side, who beat off competition from Saudi Arabia to get a deal over the line.

Fellow Turkish club Besiktas had also been in the running, however they could not match the final offer on the table.

Trabzonspor president Ertugrul Dogan told Turkish newspaper Fanatik: “He (Salah) is a world star.



“We needed a player like him. It will be great. May it be beneficial for our community.

“We accelerated the transfer process when other teams withdrew. I had a meeting with Salah and his agent.



“It was a very professional, respectful meeting where both sides understood each other and there was no difficulty. We met for about 10 days.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“We are trying to send a message to everyone and to Europe that Trabzonspor can bring whoever it wants to Trabzon.

“Our recent success is being talked about all over Turkey and Europe.”

Sports.title: Under-fire Fifa boss Gianni Infantino APOLOGISES after trying to flog the World Cup but will STAY as president
Sports.content:
FIFA chief Gianni Infantino has APOLOGISED for his deplorable efforts to flog the World Cup – but has defiantly vowed to fight on.

The 56-year-old admitted mistakes were made over the handling of the proposed scheme to sell shares of the World Cup enterprise to private investors.



In a joint letter signed by Infantino and secretary general Mattias Grafstrom, senior officials said: “We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again.

“We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.



“With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting.”

The letter confirmed that Fifa will carry out an internal review.



The findings will then be presented to the Fifa Council at its next scheduled meeting.

Officials insisted the proposal would have required approval from both Fifa’s 211 member associations and the Fifa Council.

They have acknowledged member associations and council members should not have felt excluded from the process.

And added that the proposal “should have been handled differently” – conceding further errors were made after details emerged to the public.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

But it has been confirmed that it has now been taken “off the table” following the controversy.

The statement also contained a strongly worded warning after confidential details of the proposal were leaked.

It said: “With the project withdrawn, Fifa will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation.”

But in spite of the apology, Fifa covered bases as they defended the legality of their actions.



They wrote: “Everything that was done, was done in full compliance with the Fifa regulatory framework.”

The letter also added unanimous backing for Infantino from Fifa’s senior leadership following a meeting in Rabat, Morocco.

They detailed how the president, secretary general, and administration spoke with “one voice and working as one team”.

With Infantino set to continue in his present role, he will not be without his critics.



Ballon d’Or winner and Uefa advisor Luis Figo slammed the president for “the lowest, most deceitful and cravenly self-interested” he has ever seen.

In a scathing critique of Fifa‘s incumbent, he concluded: “It is too late to save his dignity but it is not too late to save football.”

Even former disgraced Fifa president Sepp Blatter publicly called for Lise Klaveness to succeed Infantino.

He admitted: “The time is right for a woman to take the lead.”

It also stated Fifa would be “granted a preferred equity stake in the Super League”, thus ensuring the power to make decisions on format and calendar changes plus the appointment of a chief executive and distribution of funds. When approached by SunSport for comment, Fifa sent links to articles posted in 2021 including Infantino’s comments to the Uefa congress and a signed statement from the Fifa boss plus the presidents of the six continental confederations refusing to recognise any unaffiliated, rival competitions.

Those publicly supporting Infantino are few to none, with Uefa president Aleksander Ceferin leading the pack.

Ceferin snubbed the World Cup final following the fiasco surrounding Folarin Balogun’s suspended red card.

And since then, Arsene Wenger has joined the ranks against Infantino.

The Fifa president broke cover for the first time on Wednesday as he was seen in Morocco for an emergency meeting.

A Mercedes containing the beleaguered supremo was seen swooping into Fifa’s African base in Rabat.



According to The Times, Infantino had been holed up in Rabat and has called senior Fifa staff to the Moroccan capital for the urgent gathering.

Sports.title: Eagle-eyed Arsenal fans convinced Vinicius Jr is joining as Instagram wiped clean just hours after crunch Real talks

Reports on the Real Madrid superstar have speculated about a possible blockbuster move to Arsenal.



The Brazilian, 26, has now caused even more of a stir after leaving his 64million followers without a post as fans are convinced it means a Premier League move is sealed.

Before wiping the slate, Vini had a whopping 788 posts with several story highlights.

Eager fans rushed to social media to comment on the whirlwind of transfer rumours.

One X user wrote: “Clearing his profile so he can post the announcement video in a Gunners shirt, it’s happening.”

Sports.title: Arsenal 1 Real Betis 3: Angry Arteta knows Arsenal doesn’t have back-to-back title winning squad after Betis horror show

Arsenal looked lacklustre as they were thumped by Real Betis in their first meaningful pre-season match.

Their behind-closed-doors friendly against MK Dons was a glorified training session, while Saturday’s 4-1 win over Girona was a simple task against second-tier opposition.



Last night’s game, though, was a real test against a fellow Champions League side—a test they failed.

There is grace in the fact that Arsenal are without a host of World Cup stars, including Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice and the injured William Saliba.

But if this match was anything to go by, Arteta will be desperate to raise the bar with some more additions.

The imminent arrival of Bruno Guimaraes – who is set to join in a £75m move – will do just that, but there is plenty of work to be done.



Reports suggest that Vinicius Junior has been offered a more lucrative contract by Real Madrid, which could scupper Arsenal’s ambitious move for the superstar.

Kepa Arrizabalaga, another example of a player who falls below the required level, was at fault for Real Betis’ first goal.

The Spaniard flapped at a corner leaving Riquelme wide open at the back post to poke home with ease.

Kepa was partially to blame for the second goal, too.



The Spaniard gifted Betis the ball with a mis-hit clearance, allowing Nelson Deossa to unleash a stunning long-range effort into the top corner.

Arteta’s newest investment, Christos Tzolis, provided a glimmer of hope for the new campaign when his perfect corner landed on the head of Piero Hincapie to pull one back for the Gunners.

But another individual error, this time a sloppy Kai Havertz pass, gave Betis the ball again before half-time, allowing Pablo Fornals to fire a third past Kepa.

Mass changes in the second half disrupted the tempo of the game as Arsenal hobbled their way to a 3-1 defeat.

But it was a stark reminder that if Arteta wants to hit a “different dimension” this season, as he has suggested, then superstar recruitment is a necessity.

Sports.title: Why Newcastle turned to Matthias Jaissle as Toon promise ‘high-energy football’ after shock Eddie Howe exit
Sports.content:
THE BOOK has closed on the most-successful era of Newcastle’s modern history.

Internally at St. James’ Park, there is huge confidence that Matthias Jaissle can make phase two of the Saudi project even more memorable.



But with a squad stripped of its top stars, the 38-year-old German will have to be better than his CV suggests to get the Mags flying high again.

The departure of Bruno Guimaraes was the latest blow in a bruising Tyneside summer. In fact, it brought to an end an agonising 12 months that began with Alexander Isak’s controversial exit.



Eddie Howe, despite spending all of the £130m they got for the Swede, failed to recover from the loss of his star striker.

Toon had lost their tune, and after last season’s underwhelming campaign, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali were the first to jump ship.



Once skipper Guimaraes set his heart on Arsenal, Howe felt, with his squad torn apart, he was no longer the man to lead Newcastle.

He opted to go with his reputation intact, ensuring he’ll always be lauded for guiding the club from 19th to two Champions League qualifications and ending a 70-year wait for silverware.

From the outside, the prospects of Jaissle achieving anything like that success fast look slim.

Work is ongoing to recruit an experienced replacement for Guimaraes, but aside from new £25.7m goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, all of Toon’s exciting incomings have been 20 or younger.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

EDDIE HOWE'S RECORD AT NEWCASTLE EDDIE HOWE will forever be a Newcastle legend after leading the Toon to their first trophy in 70 years. But that Carabao Cup win, and two Champions League qualifications, weren’t enough to keep everyone happy on Tyneside. Here is Howe’s Newcastle record: Premier League 2021-22 – 11th (19th when he took over) 2022-23 – 4th 2023-24 – 7th 2024-25 – 5th 2025-26 – 12th Trophies won Carabao Cup 2024-25

While he arrives with several trophies already on his CV, Jaissle faces some task leading Newcastle’s new young guns and remaining old guard back to the big time.

So just what has convinced Newcastle’s Saudi PIF owners, who boldly aim to be title challengers by 2030, that he can ensure the next chapter of their reign will be a hit?

His coaching career first took him to Denmark and then Red Bull Salzburg’s academy after playing for Hoffenheim in his homeland.

FC Liefering provided him with a first senior job before he landed the top one at Salzburg in 2021.



Steeped in the Red Bull philosophy of high pressing, possession and direct play, it did not take long to win over supporters.

Jaissle won the double in his first season and retained the league the next, working with the likes of Manchester United’s Benjamin Sesko, while reaching the Champions League knockouts.

Two years later he moved to the Saudi Pro League and Al-Ahli, transforming them into one of Asia’s top sides, and leading them to back-to-back AFC Champions League crowns.



Jaissle, who added a Saudi Super Cup to his resume, style has also evolved.

Salzburg was built around the Ralf Rangnick inspired narrow 4-4-2 with wingers coming inside. But it was an attacking 4-2-3-1 he often adopted at Al Ahli.

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson is a fan.

He said: “Matthias’ leadership style and football philosophy are strongly aligned with our sporting vision. His teams play high-energy football and we could feel his passion during all of our discussions throughout the recruitment process.”

But we could well see change again. For Jaissle, inspired by bits from all of the top coaches rather than just one, precise formations come second to principles about style.



Jaissle’s experience working in multi-cultural dressing rooms will be key in pulling the Toon plan together.

He unofficially arrived at the La Manga training camp on Saturday, giving him a week to work with his men before the upcoming friendly in Valencia.

But with a young squad re-energised despite the loss of its big hitters, don’t expect Jaissle to have overloaded his players with tactics.



Discussing his philosophy previously, he said: “You really have to take care that you don’t have too much information. This is a big challenge. As a manager or coach, you know so much about tactics, but you cannot just give everything to the players. You have to really take care not to overwhelm them.”

Despite the big-name exits, the prospect of spearheading a team of young starlets and turning the page in Newcastle’s Saudi story is what appeals most to him.

He said: “I believe there is enormous potential within this squad and throughout the football club. I am excited to work with the players, staff and leadership team to help take the club forward.”

Jaissle will certainly bring new energy and ideas. And with the club back on track financially, there is a feeling this changing of the guard is the start of exciting times.

Head honcho Wilson added: “Matthias has consistently demonstrated an ability to improve players, build cohesive teams and create elite performance environments in his coaching career.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“His successes at Salzburg and Al-Ahli underline his ability to deliver results while developing a clear football identity.

“We believe he is uniquely positioned to build on the strong foundations already in place and help take Newcastle United forward.”

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino issues grovelling apology for botched World Cup plot after crisis meeting

Gianni Infantino has been under fire for the last week after FIFA's controversial plan to sell off its competitions, including the World Cup, to private investors came to light

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino has been forced to apologise (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

Grovelling Gianni Infantino has apologised for attempting to sell the World Cup, confirming that the controversial plan has been SCRAPPED. Infantino has faced intense backlash since FIFA announced last week - after media reports broke the news - a proposal for its competitions to be sold to private investors, sparking anger among the football community at all levels.

‌



UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments if the plan was allowed to go ahead, while FIFA chief Arsene Wenger spoke out against it. A crisis meeting was held in Morocco on Wednesday amid the unrelenting criticism and constant leaks regarding the plans.

‌



And now Infantino has admitted defeat with an apology - although he plans to fight on and remain FIFA President, despite widespread calls for him to resign. A letter signed by both Infantino and the FIFA General Secretary, Mattias Grafstrom, reads: "We acknowledge that errors were also made after the proposal was leaked to media.

‌



"We sincerely apologise for these errors and commit to them not happening again. With this in mind, we will conduct a necessary review, and a report will be presented to the FIFA Council at its next scheduled meeting."

The letter adds that Grafstrom and FIFA's Management Board 'reaffirm their full support' for Infantino, who's up for re-election next March. It goes on to say: "With the project withdrawn, FIFA will no longer tolerate any attacks on its integrity, good governance and due process and will take all necessary measures to protect and safeguard its name and reputation."

‌



Meanwhile, FIFA say that its leadership held a constructive and positive meeting in Rabat. It comes after a bombshell report claiming that Infantino had offered Morocco the chance to host 2030 World Cup final - which they're co-hosting with Spain and Portugal - if they agreed to his plan.

Should Gianni Infantino resign? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



Any federations who backed the scheme were told that they would receive £30million, a portion of which would be available in January if they responded positively by a September deadline. Infantino was even accused of bribery by the president of the Jordan FA, who hit out on social media.

Prince Ali bin Al Hussein posted: "We pride ourselves in Jordan in upholding ethical values. We did not endorse him before and certainly will not now. But the whole situation amounts to blackmail and we refuse to give in to that."
