Sports.title: Gasly: F1 driving is no longer about pushing to the limit in corners | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s new rules have fundamentally changed the art of driving, according to Pierre Gasly.

The Alpine driver said the overriding need to drive as quickly as possible through every corner no longer applies as saving energy has become so important.

Many F1 drivers have vehemently criticised the series’ new rules. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali said he had urged them to keep their comments “constructive.”

Gasly was reluctant to criticise the regulations but said the series has gone “too far” in reducing the performance of its combustion engines compared to the batteries. He said this has forced strange compromises on the drivers.

“Whenever you get the full power output out of a corner, it’s a very unique feeling, something that I’ll never get tired of,” he told Autocar. “Now the whole battery story this year, I’m not going to get into too much detail, because I’m not a big fan myself of all of that and I don’t want to get too bold about all these topics with the battery, et cetera.

“But I think it went a bit too far because now we have a lot to manage, actually. You’ve got to be driving efficiently, which doesn’t mean necessarily going as fast as you can through all the corners.

“There is some sort of management and understanding of which corners need to be pushed absolutely to one hundred percent or which ones are you actually better off just taking a bit of margin in your driving and the way you go back on power to get a better lap time out of it.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“Which, if you ask me, from the day I started go-karting at six years old there’s been only one rule: when you’re behind the wheel you just go as fast as you can through the corners. I think that’s the way it should be.”

Despite the power deficit the cars suffer on some tracks, particularly high-speed courses such as Spa and Silverstone, Gasly said the current chassis are still capable of taking corners at impressive speeds.

“We still have a lot of load and downforce on the car,” he said. “So in Maggotts and Becketts [at Silverstone] you’re going through these corners at like 270kph, 280kph, we’re getting up to 5G, it’s definitely a feeling which you don’t get anywhere else than in a Formula 1 car.”

Formula 1

Sports.title: Canelo Refuses To Give Crawford Full Credit For Defeat
Sports.content:
“You cannot control the results,” Alvarez said. “Even when you do everything good, things don’t go your way. I learned that. Sometimes we forget the bases, and I forgot the bases in that fight,” said Canelo to CBS Mornings about his loss to Crawford. “Mentally, I was not there. I did everything correct in the training camp, but mentally I was not there. I learned that. If I’m going to still fighting, I need to be there mentally and physically.”

Alvarez’s explanation puts the spotlight on his own performance rather than Crawford’s. He did not point to injuries, problems in training camp or controversial judging. Instead, he argued that his mindset kept him from performing at the standard he expected of himself.

Not everyone will accept that explanation. Crawford spent months crafting a game plan, executed it with discipline and repeatedly beat Alvarez to the punch. His speed, timing and ring IQ played a major role in one of the biggest victories of his career. Because of that, some fans will view Alvarez’s comments as an honest assessment of his own shortcomings, while others will see them as an attempt to soften the impact of a clear defeat.

One thing is certain: Canelo does not believe the fight reflected his best version. Combined with his recent comments about wanting a lucrative rematch, it is clear he still believes he can produce a different result if the two ever meet again.

Canelo still has to get past WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli on October 31 for a Crawford rematch to remain a realistic possibility. Even if he defeats Mbilli, it’s far from certain Turki Alalshikh will want to finance a second fight after last September’s disappointing first meeting. Crawford spent much of the night boxing cautiously, tying Canelo up whenever he closed the distance, while Alvarez faded after the sixth round. Given the lukewarm reaction to the bout, Turki may decide his money is better spent on fresher matchups rather than revisiting a fight that failed to meet expectations.

Sports.title: Remembering Boxing’s Most Unusual Heavyweights
Sports.content:
Dallas Cowboys defensive end Ed “Too Tall” Jones brought NFL fame into the boxing ring during the late 1970s. He finished 6-0 after stepping away from football, although many questioned the quality of his opposition. Jones was knocked down in his professional debut before escaping with a heavily booed majority decision over Abraham Meneses. Only one of his six opponents owned a winning record. Following a first-round knockout of Ricky Gonzalez in his final bout, Jones returned to the Cowboys.

Eric “Butterbean” Esch became one of boxing’s biggest attractions during the 1990s thanks to his enormous size and knockout power. Known as “The King of the Four Rounders,” Butterbean finished with a 77-10-4 record and 58 knockouts. His most memorable performance came in 2002 against former heavyweight champion Larry Holmes. Fighting ten rounds for the only time in his career, Butterbean scored a knockdown in the final round before losing a unanimous decision in the 53-year-old Holmes’ farewell fight.

Chicago’s Craig Bodzianowski won his first 17 professional fights before a motorcycle accident resulted in the amputation of his right leg below the knee. Refusing to walk away from boxing, he returned with a prosthetic limb and eventually challenged WBA cruiserweight champion Robert Daniels. Bodzianowski lost the decision after suffering severe facial damage, yet simply reaching a world title fight under those circumstances remains one of boxing’s most remarkable comeback stories.

None of these men became heavyweight champions remembered for championship reigns. Instead, each earned a lasting place in boxing history because their careers unfolded in ways few other fighters could match.

Sports.title: Cassius Clay vs Doug Jones 1963 The Night A Future Champion Was Pushed To His Limit
Sports.content:
Despite his unbeaten streak, skepticism remained. His speed and reflexes had overwhelmed previous opponents, yet critics remained unconvinced those strengths would survive against a seasoned contender who refused to be intimidated. His habit of pulling straight back with his hands low also invited scrutiny. If Jones timed those defensive lapses, many believed the young contender’s shortcomings would finally cost him.

Clay intensified the spotlight. He first predicted a sixth-round stoppage before changing it to the fourth after spotting a newspaper photograph of Jones reading a book titled The Rise and Fall of Cassius Clay. He mocked Jones throughout the promotion. Jones responded calmly, saying Clay’s boasting increased both purses while maintaining he would win.

Jones immediately justified the pre-fight concerns. He landed clean right hands early, repeatedly timing Clay as he leaned straight back, and absorbed the favorite’s attacks without flinching. When the fourth round passed without the promised knockout, the Madison Square Garden crowd greeted Clay with loud boos. The final rounds remained competitive before Clay finished with a stronger burst of activity to secure a unanimous decision.

The verdict settled little. Two officials scored the fight five rounds to four with one even for Clay, while the referee had him comfortably ahead. Many ringside writers disagreed, with one media poll producing more scorecards for Jones than Clay. The disputed result, combined with Jones’ performance throughout the contest, left many wondering whether Clay was truly ready for Sonny Liston.

History answered those questions quickly. Clay stopped Henry Cooper three months later before defeating Liston in one of boxing’s greatest upsets. Jones never received his own title opportunity despite pushing the future champion harder than almost anyone during his rise. For one night inside Madison Square Garden, Doug Jones forced the boxing world to question whether the sport’s loudest prospect was truly destined to become heavyweight champion.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Accuses Jaron Ennis Of Targeting Injured Josh Kelly To Avoid Vergil Ortiz Jr.
Sports.content:
“If Boots decides to fight Kelly and take advantage of Kelly being cut and everything, then that’s kind of showing me that you really don’t want to fight Virgil,” Robert said to Sean Zittel. “The fighter will probably do it because he’s a fighter. He’s a warrior, and he’ll probably get the biggest payday in his career, and he could lose to anybody else because, let’s be real, Kelly might not be the best in the division. So, they’re going after him to take advantage of that opportunity to get another belt under his belt.”

The veteran trainer dismissed any suggestion that his fighter needs an interim bout before pursuing the division’s biggest name. Ortiz is already back in camp. He said the former interim champion wants Ennis next.

“We don’t need a tuneup. We want to go straight into Boots,” Garcia said. “If Boots decides to go after him and take advantage of that big old cut, then that’s the way they’re going to do it. I can’t force them either.”

Ennis has repeatedly spoken about adding more world titles, with Kelly and WBC champion Sebastian Fundora mentioned as possible opponents. Garcia rejected that explanation, insisting the larger fight sits across the ring.

“No, that’s a lie. He doesn’t want to fight Virgil,” Garcia said. “The fight against Virgil is three times bigger when it comes to his payday, to a meaningful fight. Nobody’s going to care because you beat Kelly or you beat Virgil. A win over somebody like Virgil means a lot more than Josh Kelly.”

Asked why he believes Ortiz wins the matchup, Garcia offered a brief reply.

“Because I know he beats him,” Garcia said. “I know he beat him.”

Sports.title: Jose Valenzuela Calls For William Zepeda Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Felicidades por la victoria. Sin duda, es otra gran pelea que me encantaría hacer. Ojalá algún día podamos compartir el ring,” Valenzuela wrote on X. Translated, Valenzuela said: “Congratulations on the victory. Without a doubt, it’s another great fight that I’d love to make. Hopefully one day we can share the ring.”

Fresh off his second-round knockout of a ring-rusty Edwin De Los Santos on June 28, Valenzuela (16-3, 10 KOs) is trying to turn that performance into another title opportunity. Before calling for Zepeda, he repeatedly called out fellow Zuffa fighter and WBO light welterweight champion Shakur Stevenson, but those public challenges gained little attention.

Matching Valenzuela with Zepeda presents a different challenge.

Zepeda is promoted by Golden Boy Promotions and competes on DAZN, while Valenzuela is now aligned with Zuffa Boxing and fights on Paramount+. Crossing promotional lines and television platforms is possible, but it usually requires a matchup with significant commercial value.

Unless one side is willing to bridge that promotional divide, Valenzuela may have to keep looking in-house for his next opportunity while Zepeda pursues bigger names at lightweight. Neither promotion has shown interest in working together yet.

Sports.title: Larry Holmes vs. Tex Cobb: A Title Fight That Never Should Have Happened
Sports.content:
The timing could hardly have been worse. Just 13 days earlier, Duk Koo Kim died from injuries sustained in his lightweight title fight with Ray Mancini. Boxing was facing intense criticism over fighter safety, and every televised bout carried added scrutiny. Holmes then defended his WBC heavyweight championship against Randall “Tex” Cobb, a durable pressure fighter whose style played directly into the champion’s strengths.

It took only a few minutes to see how difficult the fight would be. Holmes established his jab immediately, keeping Cobb at the end of his punches while the challenger trudged forward looking for openings that rarely appeared.

Holmes took control almost immediately, repeatedly snapping Cobb’s head back with straight punches while staying comfortably out of danger. Cobb kept marching forward, but each attempt to close the distance brought more punishment than success.

Before long, the championship no longer felt competitive. Cobb’s determination never wavered, yet he had no answer for Holmes’ speed, timing or control of the distance.

Howard Cosell reached that conclusion as the rounds wore on. Working the ABC broadcast, he repeatedly questioned why referee Steve Crosson allowed the fight to continue. Cosell called it a total mismatch and wondered whether the prolonged punishment damaged boxing’s public image. His frustration became one of the night’s defining storylines, and the bout is widely remembered as the final straw that led him to leave professional boxing broadcasts.

Nothing about the performance was reckless. Holmes avoided unnecessary risks and dominated virtually every round. Cobb spent most of the fight trying to get inside, only to run into the jab again and again.

Yet that same superiority turned the fight into an ordeal for many viewers. Every clean jab and unanswered combination reinforced the same question: when does a championship fight stop being competitive enough to continue?

After 15 rounds, the scorecards reflected the one-sided action. Holmes retained his title by unanimous decision. Cobb never touched the canvas despite absorbing hundreds of punches. His courage was beyond question, though the wisdom of allowing him to remain in the fight drew severe scrutiny.

Holmes-Cobb became far more than another title defense. It showed what can happen when a champion operates on a completely different level from his challenger. Coming less than two weeks after Duk Koo Kim’s death, the fight also renewed questions about when a referee should stop a one-sided beating.

Sports.title: Teofimo Lopez Reveals Private Conversation With Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Teofimo Lopez already has a long-term target in mind beyond his August 22 challenge for Rolando Romero’s WBA welterweight title. The former two-division champion revealed he recently spoke with Devin Haney and believes the pair are on separate courses toward an eventual fight for the undisputed welterweight championship.

“I told Devin Haney about this,” Teofimo said to Sean Zittel. “I told Devin Haney, ‘Me and you, we’re going to go two different sides, but we’re going to meet at the end for undisputed at once.’ He said, ‘All right, those are your words.’ I said, ‘I’m keeping them. Let’s get it going.’ So, I think right now it’s more so who wins September 12th, but mainly right now focus on August 22nd. We’ll go from there. I don’t think I’m going to see Haney until the end.”

Lopez made it clear he is in no rush to face Haney. His preference is for both champions to continue collecting titles before meeting with every major belt on the line.



Teofimo also believes he will be a better fighter by the time that meeting arrives. Asked if he can eventually solve Haney’s movement and back-foot style, he expressed no doubts. “Absolutely. You just got to practice. You got to practice on all those fundamentals. That’s it. I’m a pure boxer when it comes to it,” said Teofimo. “Coming forward has been looked at as a flaw of mine, but flaws are meant to happen so that you can fix them.” Teofimo has repeatedly identified becoming the undisputed welterweight champion before the 2028 Olympic Games as one of his biggest career goals. Rolly remains the immediate obstacle, while Haney continues building his own position atop the division. If both champions continue winning over the next several years, Lopez believes he and Haney will eventually meet in one of the biggest fights available at 147 pounds. Share via: Facebook

Sports.title: Staging Joshua vs. Fury in New York Is a Massive Streaming Gamble
Sports.content:
The strategy hinges on an ambitious corporate thesis: streaming platforms need live events that capture prime-time American viewership. By staging the event on a Friday night in Manhattan, Netflix can target prime-time viewers across North and South America while treating the British audience as a secondary consideration.

The strategy also carries obvious risk. A Friday night main event in New York would push the fight into the early hours of Saturday morning for viewers in Britain. Organizers are effectively betting that fans will adjust their schedules rather than reject a bout many expected to unfold at Wembley.

“It’s a bloody shame, quite frankly,” Simon Jordan said on talkSPORT. “I know that MSG is a legendary arena, but not for two British fighters in a generational fight that people want to see. But I guess he who pays the piper calls the tune.”

Jordan’s criticism goes beyond nostalgia. Joshua and Fury became global stars by filling arenas and stadiums across Britain, and Wembley always felt like the natural home for the fight. Passing up the prospect of a 90,000-seat crowd in favor of a 20,000-seat arena in Manhattan signals that global streaming economics now carry more influence than staging the event where demand has been strongest for years.

If Netflix succeeds, the move may reshape how boxing’s biggest events are scheduled for the streaming era. If British television audiences fall sharply because of the timing, executives may discover that maximizing global reach can come at the expense of the audience that made the fight possible in the first place.

Ghana News.title: GAF observes maiden Omane Boamah memorial lecture
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Armed Forces on Tuesday observed the maiden annual memorial public lecture in honour of the late Defence Minister Dr Edward Kofi Omane Boamah at the Burma Camp in Accra.

Dr Omane Boamah and seven other public officials lost their lives in a military helicopter crash at Adansi Akrofuom in the Ashanti Region on August 6th, 2025, while on a national assignment.

Among the dignitaries that grace the maiden annual memorial public lecture were Vice President Professor Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, Dr Julius Debrah, Chief of Staff at the Presidency and Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson, the Finance Minister and Acting Defence Minister.

Also in attendance were service chiefs and old students from the Pope John Senior High School and Junior Seminary, Koforidua where the late Defence Minister schooled.

The maiden public lecture, which was chaired by Nana Dr Emmanuel Adu-Sarkodee, the President of the Ghana Employers’ Association and Akwamu Manwerehene, had two main speakers.

Reverend Father Dr Ebenezer Akesseh, the Parish Priest of Christ the King Parish of the Catholic Church, Accra, delivered the first lecture on the topic “Selfless Leadership in Public Service: Lessons from the Life and Legacy of the late Dr Omane Boamah”.

Whereas Professor Kwasi Appeaning Addo, a former Director of the Institute of Environment and Sanitation Studies, Department of Marine and Fisheries Science, University of Ghana, delivered the second lecture on the topic “Accra Beyond the Floods: Rethinking Enforcement, Urban Planning and Community Resilience”.

Rev. Dr Akesseh in his presentation described public service as a vocation and a divine calling to serve humanity rather than a profession pursued for personal gain.

He reiterated that the late Dr Omane Boamah exemplified servant leadership by dedicating his talents, medical expertise and political career to the service of Ghana, adding that Dr Omane Boamah consistently placed the needs of others above his own interests.

Rev. Dr Akesseh cited an instance where the late minister interrupted his journey to personally assist a woman in distress and ensured she received urgent medical care, demonstrating that compassion must always be accompanied by action.

He said Dr Omane Boamah viewed leadership as a moral responsibility rooted in integrity, humility and accountability; declaring that throughout his career, the late Dr Boamah earned the trust of his colleagues and the public by remaining transparent, rejecting corruption and making decisions based on national interest rather than personal or political advantage.

Prof. Addo in his presentation made a call to action for the Accra Beyond the Floods Equation, saying in honouring the legacy of the late Defence Minister, a climate resilient Accra could be realised by combining disciplined urban order with progressive engineering.

This would secure the capital against flood disaster, building on its early foundational work, by leading national environmental investigations and tree planting campaigns, the vision to transition Accra from reactive crisis management to a highly regulated sustainable city, he said.

He stressed that the proposed Accra flood resilience strategy could integrate natural infrastructure; AI driven enforcement and community led action to transition into a secure and sustainable capital.

Prof. Addo said the transformation of Ghana’s capital from a flood prone city to a climate resilient one, could not be achieved through isolated efforts, but required a unified front where policy, tradition, advocacy and civic duty intersected to secure the city’s future.

“The mandate for each stakeholder group is clear and immediate. To our policy makers, please lead with courage and integrity and enforce without fear or favor. Utilise the digital planning and GIS mapping to permanently lock out unauthorized construction in our towers,” he said.

He urged the nation’s traditional leaders to protect natural purpose by acting as strong custodians of their lands, refusing the sale of wetlands and flood plains to developers, to ensure social accountability, ensuring that ecological zoning laws were respected at every local level.

Prof. Addo encouraged civil society and the media to champion truth and equity, as well as maintain continuous independence oversight on the prosecution of corrupt planning officials.

He also urged them to drive public education by keeping climate adaptation and waste management sensitisation at the forefront of public discourse.

“To our citizens, stop the practice of damping solid and plastic waste into their dreams. Take active charge of your neighborhood’s cleanliness,” calling on people to volunteer as community-led early warning and disaster response teams, refusing the purchase of land in flood plains.

He appealed to them to act as whistle blowers on illegal development that threatened their community’s safety; declaring that this was their collective action.

Prof. Addo stated that “either we continue down the path of a chaotic expansion and recurrent disaster, or we can choose the path of structural discipline, environmental harmony and systemic progress,” calling on all to collaborate to build a proud order.

Ghana News.title: REGSEC to begin fresh demolitions at Laboma, Agbogbloshie to curb flooding
Ghana News.content:
The Greater Accra Regional Security Council (REGSEC) is set to begin another phase of demolition exercises next week at Laboma and Agbogbloshie, targeting structures built on waterways as part of ongoing efforts to reduce flooding in Accra.

The exercise follows recent clean-up campaigns, desilting of drains and earlier demolitions carried out after the devastating June 29 floods that affected several parts of the capital.

Speaking after touring a number of Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies (MMDAs), the Greater Accra Regional Minister, Linda Ocloo, said the government remains determined to reclaim waterways and remove illegal structures contributing to persistent flooding.

She explained that the exercise forms part of a broader strategy to restore buffer zones, improve drainage infrastructure and minimise the risk of future floods in the city.

According to the Minister, authorities have identified several unauthorised structures that will have to be removed to allow for the restoration of waterways and improve the free flow of stormwater.

"We have noticed that a lot of the buildings must come down and so we will do a major demolition over there, hopefully next week. We want to create the buffer like we said. We can see that the refuse was caused by the squatters over there. Once we clear the place, we wouldn’t have issues there," Ms Ocloo said.

She reaffirmed the government's commitment to strictly enforcing planning regulations and removing structures that obstruct waterways as part of long-term measures to address flooding in the Greater Accra Region.

Ghana News.title: Social media, drug abuse fuelling student indiscipline – Deputy Education Minister
Ghana News.content:
Dr Clement Apaak, Deputy Education Minister.

The Deputy Minister for Education, Dr Clement Apaak, has identified social media, the misuse of mobile phones and the growing abuse of narcotics and other unapproved substances as major factors driving indiscipline among students.

His remarks come in the wake of an incident at Obuasi Senior High Technical School in the Ashanti Region, where students allegedly attacked the school's headmaster over claims that a baby's body had been buried on the school premises.

Speaking on Citi FM on Wednesday, August 5, Dr Apaak said student misconduct was being fuelled by a combination of influences, including unrestricted exposure to inappropriate online content and increasing peer pressure.

He explained that many young people are constantly exposed to disturbing behaviour on social media platforms, which can create the false impression that such actions carry little or no consequences.

"Some of the issues that came up, and I believe some to be true, are the negative influence of social media and the abuse of the modern cell phone," he said.

According to the Deputy Minister, students are increasingly consuming content that normalises unacceptable behaviour, making them more likely to imitate what they see.

"Students are able to see all manner of behaviours, no matter how condemnable and abhorrent, both from within the jurisdiction and beyond. And somehow they begin to get a feeling that they can also act in such manners and get away with it," he stated.

Dr Apaak also expressed concern over the increasing use of narcotics and unauthorised substances among young people, describing it as a growing challenge that extends beyond senior high schools.

"We also have the incessant danger of the use of narcotics and other unapproved medical substances. This is a very serious issue that is also plaguing our youth," he said.

He noted that the problem affects students across different levels of the education system, including junior high schools and tertiary institutions, and warned that some products sold as energy drinks may contain harmful mixtures capable of influencing behaviour.

"You see them holding these energy drinks, and you might think that it is just an energy drink. But that is a potent concoction of a combination of all kinds of substances," he added.

Ghana News.title: IMF urges BoG to end quasi-fiscal activitiess after GH¢22bn DGPP losses
Ghana News.content:
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has urged the Bank of Ghana (BoG) to end quasi-fiscal activities following losses recorded under the Domestic Gold Purchase Programme (DGPP).

The Fund said the DGPP recorded losses of GHS22 billion in 2025, equivalent to about 1.5 per cent of Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP), weakening the central bank’s financial position.

The IMF said the losses, together with other factors, increased the BoG’s negative equity position to 6.7 per cent of GDP by the end of 2025.

It said safeguarding the independence and credibility of the central bank required the permanent cessation of quasi-fiscal operations and the full transfer of the DGPP to GoldBod.

The DGPP was introduced to strengthen Ghana’s gold and foreign exchange reserves through the purchase of gold from local miners.

Although the programme contributed to higher reserves, the Fund said it also imposed significant financial costs on the central bank.

In July 2026, the Government, the BoG and GoldBod signed an agreement transferring all DGPP activities from the central bank to GoldBod.

Under the arrangement, GoldBod will assume responsibility for purchasing gold and meeting all operational costs, while the BoG will focus on its core mandate.

The IMF welcomed the transfer, stating that it would eliminate future financial risks from the central bank’s balance sheet and enhance transparency in the management of the programme.

The Fund also called for the recapitalisation of the central bank, noting that a strong financial position was essential to maintaining price stability and confidence in the economy.

An independent audit of the DGPP is underway, with its findings expected later this year.

Ghana News.title: Korle Bu emergency cases surge from 70 to over 100 daily
Ghana News.content:
The Accident and Emergency Department of the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital is recording a sharp rise in daily patient attendance, with cases increasing from about 50 and 70 to more than 100.

Dr Henry Bulley, Head of the Department, said the unit, which had a 50-bed capacity, now received about 100 patients daily, with numbers sometimes exceeding that figure.

In an interview with the Ghana News Agency, Dr Bulley attributed the increase to rising trauma and non-trauma cases, including strokes, sudden loss of consciousness, severe diabetic complications, kidney diseases, domestic injuries and road traffic crashes.

He said, except for women in labour and children with non-trauma medical conditions who were managed at specialised units, most emergency cases were referred to the department.

Dr Bulley said while trauma cases continued to increase, medical emergencies had become particularly concerning.

“Previously, adults with malaria would simply visit clinics with fever, headaches and body pains, get tested, treated and go home. Now they are arriving unconscious, and many also present with severe kidney injuries,” he said.

He said health professionals were yet to establish the exact causes of the trend but stressed the need for further scientific investigation.

“We are asking ourselves what is happening in the system. Could it be due to the effects of illegal mining activities? The cases are not coming from Accra alone.

“Even the food we eat and the water we drink come from different parts of the country. It is something that should be studied properly before conclusions are drawn,” he said.

Dr Bulley also expressed concern about the steady rise in road traffic accident cases recorded at the hospital.

He said data from the department showed that emergency attendances during the first six months of recent years had remained high, with road traffic cases recording an upward trend.

The department attended to 7,781 emergency patients by the end of June 2026, compared with 7,108 in the same period in 2025, 7,910 in 2024 and 7,362 in 2023.

Road traffic accident cases accounted for 553 of this year’s attendances, representing 7.11 per cent of all emergency cases. This compared with 379 cases (5.33 per cent) in 2025, 368 cases (4.65 per cent) in 2024 and 384 cases (5.22 per cent) in 2023.

Despite the increase in accident cases, Dr Bulley said improvements in emergency care had contributed to a reduction in the proportion of deaths among accident victims.

Departmental data showed that 10 accident-related deaths were recorded by the end of June this year, representing a mortality rate of 1.81 per cent, compared with seven deaths (1.85 per cent) during the same period in 2025.

The department recorded 12 deaths (3.26 per cent) in 2024 and seven deaths (1.82 per cent) in 2023.

Dr Bulley attributed the improved outcomes to increased availability of emergency physicians and specialised emergency nurses.

He said continued improvements in emergency medicine had strengthened the department’s ability to stabilise critically injured patients and improve survival rates.

Dr Bulley identified festive periods, long public holidays and school vacations as peak periods for emergency cases.

“When children are on vacation, we see more injuries involving them. During Easter, Christmas, New Year and other holidays, the numbers also go up,” he said.

Dr Bulley attributed many crashes during such periods to increased travel, alcohol consumption, substance use and unsafe driving practices.

“We mix celebrations with risky modes of transport. The adrenaline goes up, people consume alcohol and other substances, and unfortunately we record more accidents during these periods,” he added.

Dr Bulley called for intensified road safety education and preventive measures to reduce injuries and ease pressure on emergency departments across the country.

Ghana News.title: Sagnarigu MUSEC imposes curfew on Damankungyili, Nyeshie following deadly clash
Ghana News.content:
The Sagnarigu Municipal Security Council (MUSEC) has imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew on Damankungyili, Nyeshie and adjoining communities in the Sagnarigu Municipality in the Northern Region.

The curfew will be in force daily from 1700 hours to 0700 hours until further notice.

This followed violent disturbances that claimed one life and left six others injured in those communities.

The decision was announced in a press statement issued after an emergency meeting by the MUSEC, held on Tuesday, to assess the security situation following the clashes between the two communities.

The statement was signed by Mr Abdulai Imoro Gong, the Chairman of the MUSEC and Sagnarigu Municipal Chief Executive and copied to the Ghana News Agency in Tamale.

The statement said the emergency meeting was convened following disturbances between the communities of Damankungyili and Nyeshie, which resulted in the death of one person and injuries to six others.

It said the Council strongly condemned the violence describing the loss of life and injuries sustained by residents as unfortunate and unacceptable.

It said the curfew was imposed in consultation with the Northern Regional Security Council as part of measures to restore calm, protect lives and property, and prevent further escalation of the conflict.

As part of the curfew, the MUSEC has also announced a total ban on the carrying of arms, ammunition and other offensive weapons within the affected communities.

The Council also directed the deployment of increased joint Police patrols to enforce the curfew and maintain law and order in the area.

It appealed to residents to comply fully with the directives and cooperate with the security agencies to ensure a quick return to peace.

It urged chiefs, elders, youth and all residents of Damankungyili and Nyeshie to remain calm and avoid actions that could inflame tensions.

It encouraged members of the public with credible information relating to the disturbances to volunteer such information to the Police to support ongoing investigations.

The statement also appealed to media organisations, especially radio stations, to exercise restraint and professionalism in their reportage to avoid inflammatory commentary capable of aggravating the security situation.

Ghana News.title: Police probe explosion at a tailings site in Aboso
Ghana News.content:
The Western Central Regional Police Command has initiated investigations into an explosion that occurred at a tailings site in Aboso in the Western Region on Tuesday, August 4, 2026.

The incident resulted in the death of three persons. Three others were injured.

This was disclosed in a statement signed by Assistant Superintendent of Police Beatrice Turkson, the Head of Public Affairs Unit, Western Central Region and copied to the Ghana News Agency.

Preliminary investigations revealed that at about 1200 hours on the day of the incident, workers of the site spotted a python and informed the owner, David Kofi Fletcher, now deceased, who reportedly arrived at the site armed with a pump-action shotgun to kill the reptile.

The statement said it suspected that after the deceased fired a shot, the pellets struck explosive materials believed to have been illegally stored at the premises, triggering the explosion.

The explosion claimed the life of the site owner; David Kofi Fletcher and two other persons identified only as Solomon and Baba.

According to the statement, three persons sustained various degrees of injury and were rushed to hospital, where they are receiving treatment.

It added that the bodies of the deceased have been deposited at the Tarkwa Municipal Hospital mortuary for preservation and autopsy.

The explosion also caused extensive damage to nearby properties, several houses within the vicinity had their window panels shattered, while six vehicles parked at a nearby washing bay had their windscreens and windows damaged.

The Minerals Commission has been notified and is collaborating with the police as investigations continued to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident, the statement said.

The Western Central Regional Police Command has expressed its deepest condolences to the bereaved families and wished those injured speedy recovery.

The Command further reminded the public that the unlawful possession, storage, handling, or sale of explosives constitutes a serious offence and posed significant risk to public safety.

It therefore urged the public to report any suspected illegal storage or handling of explosives to the nearest police station.

Ghana News.title: Seven casualties recorded in fiery multi-vehicle crash on Accra-Kumasi Highway
Ghana News.content:
Seven lives were lost in a multiple-vehicle collision that triggered a fire outbreak at Birimso Bridge on the N6 Accra-Kumasi Highway in the Eastern Region.

The accident involved a fuel tanker, a Mitsubishi Pick-Up with registration number GE 8602-17, a KIA Sorento with registration number GT 8601-14, and an STC bus with registration number GS 7050-22.

A statement issued by the Eastern Regional Fire Command and signed by Divisional Officer Grade III (DOIII) Ohemeng Aaron, Regional Public Relations Officer, said the casualties comprised two females and five males.

According to the statement, the fuel tanker, the STC bus and the Mitsubishi Pick-Up were completely destroyed by the fire, while the KIA Sorento sustained extensive damage.

Firefighters from the Bunso Fire Station, led by Assistant Divisional Officer Grade I (ADOI) Samuel Doe, were dispatched to the scene and worked to contain the blaze. Personnel from the Suhum Municipal Fire Station, under the leadership of ADOI Moses Quaye, provided additional support to bring the fire under control.

The statement said officers from the Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) of the Ghana Police Service at Kibi also responded to the incident to assist with traffic management and investigations.

The Ghana National Fire Service urged motorists and other road users to cooperate with emergency responders as efforts continued to fully extinguish the fire and secure the accident scene.

The cause of the collision is yet to be established, the statement added.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Trump administration refunds $100bn in tariffs struck down by Supreme Court
World.content:
Move comes after the US Supreme Court struck down many of Trump’s sweeping levies in February.

United States President Donald Trump’s administration has refunded about $100bn in tariffs since the nation’s top court ruled against its use of emergency powers to impose duties on dozens of trade partners, according to customs officials.

The Trump administration collected about $166bn from US importers before the US Supreme Court struck down a large portion of the president’s tariff regime in a 6-3 ruling in February.

In a court filing on Tuesday, the US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) disclosed that it had returned more than three-quarters of $128.68bn in tariff revenues earmarked as “potential and certified refunds”.

“CBP’s financial accounting system receives updates from Treasury that indicate these CBP certified refunds are being regularly dispersed,” Brandon Lord, executive director of CBP’s Trade Policy and Programs directorate, said in the filing with the US Court of International Trade.

In its ruling, the US Supreme Court found that Trump exceeded his authority when he invoked the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA) to impose fentanyl-related tariffs on Canada, Mexico and China, and broader “reciprocal” tariffs on more than 90 countries.

Trump angrily denounced the ruling at the time, branding the six justices who sided against him “fools” and “lapdogs” for the Democratic Party.

The ruling did not nullify Trump’s tariffs on specific industries invoked under the 1962 Trade Expansion Act, leaving intact duties on goods including steel, automobiles and copper.



Following the Supreme Court’s decision, the US Court of International Trade in March ruled that companies affected by the invalidated tariffs should be refunded.

Trump has continued to roll out new tariffs since the Supreme Court’s ruling.

Last month, his administration announced levies of 10-12.5 percent on imports from dozens of countries that officials claim have not taken sufficient action to combat forced labour.

On Monday, a group of 25 US states, including New York, California, Arizona and Colorado, filed a legal challenge against the latest tariffs, calling the measures a pretext to re-impose the duties struck down in February.

World.title: How Gambian women are restoring the mangroves protecting Banjul
World.content:
The coastal trees provide a living for the women, who plant and care for them, and shield the island capital from erosion and flooding.

Banjul, The Gambia – At dawn, before the heat settles over the coast, Fatou Jarjue waits for the tide to retreat.

She pulls on her gloves and socks, steps into the muddy edge of the Tanbi Wetland and pushes her wooden canoe through narrow channels surrounded by tangled mangrove roots. Inside the canoe sit empty pans waiting to be filled, not with oysters today, but with crabs hiding beneath the surface.

The life of this mother of one is inseparable from the wetland she navigates each day. The mangroves – salt-tolerant coastal trees that protect shorelines from erosion and flooding – provide the oysters, crabs and fish that sustain her family’s livelihood while serving as a natural barrier against erosion and flooding for her coastal community.

Her brother, Musa, trails behind in a smaller canoe whenever he can, keeping watch as she moves deeper into the mangrove channels. On days when he is busy elsewhere, Jarjue ventures into the wetland alone.

For generations, women around the Tanbi Wetland have depended on these waters for survival. Jarjue still does. But unlike previous generations, she also spends part of her time restoring the ecosystem that has sustained her family for decades.

Only months earlier, these waterways were filled with women collecting oysters attached to mangrove roots. With the arrival of The Gambia’s rainy season, oyster harvesting pauses, forcing many women to turn to crabs and fishing until the shellfish season reopens.

For the 34-year-old, the change in her daily catch is temporary. Her commitment to restoring the mangroves is not.



“I have restored more than 5,000 mangroves since last year,” she told Al Jazeera.

Raised in the mangroves

Jarjue grew up in Ndangan, a small settlement of about 300 people located roughly 2km (1.2 miles) from Banjul, the capital of The Gambia. Like many children in the community, she grew up with the rhythms of the wetland.

At just 12 years old, she began following her mother into the mangroves, learning how to harvest oysters and catch crabs and fish.

The forest was both a classroom and a source of income.

Over the years, Jarjue watched the environment around her change. Rising seas, coastal erosion and changing weather patterns began threatening the coastline her community depends on.

Instead of only taking from the wetland, she decided to help rebuild it.

Today, she returns regularly not only to harvest but also to inspect young seedlings, replace damaged plants and monitor areas where restoration is needed.

“The mangroves are part of our lives,” she said.

For Jarjue, conservation is not separate from survival. The healthier the mangroves become, the stronger the future of her community.

A season’s wait

As Jarjue paddles deeper into the wetland, oysters cling to the roots of the mangroves. They are large, growing and ready for harvest in another season. She leaves them untouched.

She points towards them proudly, knowing that protecting them now will mean a better harvest later.

Although crab harvesting provides income during the rainy season, oysters remain the more profitable catch. A milk-can measure of oysters sells for about 100 dalasis ($1.34), and demand at local markets is higher.

“Oysters are difficult to harvest,” Jarjue explained. “But that is where the money is.”

The annual closure of oyster harvesting during the rainy season is sometimes misunderstood as a warning that oysters become poisonous at that time of year.

But marine scientist Dawda Saine says the reason is more complex and is rooted in conservation, ecology and food safety.

The closure forms part of The Gambia’s Oyster and Cockle Co-management Plan, which allows oyster stocks time to regenerate, reproduce and grow while reducing pressure on the resource.

“We don’t close the season because oysters are poisonous,” Saine told Al Jazeera. “We close it to protect the resource and because, during the rains, oysters filter everything in the water, including increased run-off, which can affect their quality, taste and safety.”



During the rainy season, increased run-off can carry waste and other materials into waterways where oysters feed by filtering water. Allowing them to remain undisturbed helps protect both the ecosystem and consumers.

For women like Jarjue, respecting the closure is an investment in the future.

Roots of survival

Jarjue is among several women in Ndangan who have become guardians of the ecosystem they depend on.

For 48-year-old Sussan Colley, the difference is visible every time she enters the wetland.

Colley has harvested oysters, fished and collected crabs since she was a teenager. She remembers when declining mangrove cover began affecting the community’s catches.

There were fewer oysters. Harvests became smaller. Families who depended on the wetland faced increasing uncertainty.

As restoration efforts expanded, Colley began noticing changes beneath the roots.

The oysters returned. They grew faster and larger. The wetland became productive again.

“The mangroves are changing our lives for the better,” she told Al Jazeera.

For Colley, restoration is also about preparing the next generation. She is teaching her children the skills she inherited from her parents while passing on another lesson: People must protect the natural systems that sustain them.

“I want them to make a livelihood from this,” she said, “but also understand the importance of the mangroves and the role they play in our lives.”

Jarjue and other women received training in mangrove restoration through a local conservation initiative supporting coastal communities in The Gambia. The programme equipped them with the skills to restore degraded mangroves, protect the ecosystems that support fisheries and strengthen their communities’ resilience to climate change.

For the women of Ndangan, the training changed how they viewed the forest, not only as a place to harvest, but also as something they have a responsibility to protect.

Banjul’s last shield

The work happening in Ndangan carries significance far beyond the settlement.

Banjul, The Gambia’s capital, is a low-lying island city facing growing threats from rising seas, coastal erosion and flooding. Experts have warned that a 1-metre (3ft-4-inch) rise in global sea levels could inundate parts of the city, increasing the urgency of protecting its remaining natural barriers.

The threat is not only a future concern. In 2022, severe flooding affected thousands of people across The Gambia, exposing the vulnerability of communities living along the coast.

For settlements surrounding the Tanbi Wetland, mangroves are more than an environmental resource. They are a natural defence system.

Rohey Malick Lowe, the mayor of Banjul, says the future of the capital is closely tied to the survival of its mangroves.

“Banjul is an island,” she told Al Jazeera. “If the mangroves disappear, it goes with the city.”

The mayor said the Banjul City Council is working to protect the capital from climate threats but acknowledged that challenges remain, including the degradation of parts of the wetland through human activities.



Supporting women like Jarjue, she said, is not just about protecting their incomes but also strengthening the city’s resilience.

“They are not only protecting their livelihoods,” Lowe said. “They are helping to protect Banjul.”

Roots of resilience

Despite their contribution, women in Ndangan still face challenges. Without reliable electricity, preserving oysters and crabs remains difficult, especially when market demand is low and harvests cannot be sold immediately.

But each day, Jarjue returns to the mangroves.

Sometimes she goes to harvest. Other times, she goes simply to check whether the trees she planted are surviving.

The work is slow. A mangrove seedling does not transform a coastline overnight. But for Jarjue, every new root represents a future she is helping build.

As the tide slowly rises, she guides her canoe back towards shore, leaving behind thousands of young mangroves she helped plant.

Months from now, she will return to harvest oysters from the same roots she is protecting today. Until then, she is content watching the forest grow.

Every new seedling is a quiet act of hope, not only for her family, but also for a city increasingly vulnerable to the rising sea.

Jarjue pauses before stepping onto dry land and looks back at the green canopy stretching across the wetland.

“Every morning I wake up and see the mangroves growing,” she said. “That gives me peace. If the mangroves disappear one day, our lives will disappear with them.”
